bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第079巻

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 79
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 79

sentences.zh: 【晉紀一】起旃蒙作噩，盡玄黓執徐，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 1] From Zhanmeng Zuoe through Xuanyi Zhixu, eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Jin, Number One] Spanning from the cyclical year Zhanmeng Zuoe through Xuanyi Zhixu—eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，呉主使光祿大夫紀陟、五官中郎將洪璆與徐紹、孫彧偕來報聘。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, the Lord of Wu sent Grandee of Splendid Happiness Ji Shi and Palace Attendant of the Five Offices Hong Qiu, together with Xu Shao and Sun Yu, to return a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the third month, the Wu ruler dispatched Ji Shi as Grandee of Splendid Happiness and Hong Qiu as Palace Attendant of the Five Offices, who traveled with Xu Shao and Sun Yu to repay a court visit.

sentences.zh: 紹行至濡須，有言紹譽中國之美者，呉主怒，追還，殺之。

translations.literal: When Shao reached Ruxu, someone reported that Shao was praising the beauty of the Central States; the Lord of Wu was enraged, recalled him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao reached Ruxu, word reached the Wu ruler that he had been extolling the Central States; enraged, the ruler had him recalled and executed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，呉改元甘露。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Wu changed the era name to Ganlu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Wu adopted Ganlu as its new reign title.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏帝加文王殊禮，進王妃曰后，世子曰太子。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Wei emperor conferred extraordinary honors on King Wen, promoted his princess consort to empress, and his heir apparent to crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Wei emperor granted King Wen of Jin extraordinary ceremonial honors, elevated his consort to queen, and named his heir crown prince.

sentences.zh: 癸未，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，呉主逼殺景皇后，遷景帝四子於呉；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Lord of Wu compelled the Jing empress to die and relocated the four sons of Emperor Jing to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Wu ruler forced the Jing empress to her death and sent Emperor Jing's four sons into exile in Wu territory.

sentences.zh: 尋又殺其長者二人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he also killed the two eldest among them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had the two eldest put to death as well.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛卯，文王卒，太子嗣爲相國、晉王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, King Wen died; the crown prince succeeded him as Chancellor of State and King of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao, King Wen died, and his crown prince succeeded him as Chancellor of State and King of Jin.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙未，大赦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day yiwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yiwei, the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以魏司徒何曾爲晉丞相；

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Wei Minister over the Masses He Zeng was appointed Chancellor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, He Zeng, formerly Wei Minister over the Masses, was made Chancellor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以驃騎將軍司馬望爲司徒。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, the Rapid Cavalry General Sima Wang was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Rapid Cavalry General Sima Wang was named Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，葬文王於崇陽陵。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, King Wen was buried at Chongyang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, King Wen was interred at Chongyang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬，呉西陵督歩闡表請呉主徙都武昌；

translations.literal: In winter, Bu Chan, superintendent of Xiling in Wu, memorialized asking the Lord of Wu to move the capital to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Bu Chan, Wu's superintendent of Xiling, petitioned the ruler to transfer the capital to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 呉主從之，使御史大夫丁固、右將軍諸葛靚守建業。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu assented and left Imperial Counselor Ding Gu and Right General Zhuge Jing to guard Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler agreed and left Imperial Counselor Ding Gu and Right General Zhuge Jing to hold Jianye.

sentences.zh: 闡，騭之子也。

translations.literal: Chan was the son of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Chan was a son of Bu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬戌，魏帝禪位於晉；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renxu, the Wei emperor abdicated the throne to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renxu, the Wei emperor ceded the throne to Jin.

sentences.zh: 甲子，出捨於金墉城。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, he departed and took up residence at Jinfeng City.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, he left the palace and withdrew to Jinfeng City.

sentences.zh: 太傅司馬孚拜辭，執帝手，流涕歔欷不自勝，曰：「臣死之日，固大魏之純臣也。」

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Fu took his leave, grasped the emperor's hand, and wept so uncontrollably that he could not compose himself, saying, "On the day I die, I shall remain a loyal subject of Great Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Fu bade farewell, took the emperor's hand, and sobbed until he could scarcely speak: "When I die, I shall still be a faithful servant of Great Wei."

sentences.zh: 丙寅，王卽皇帝位，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the king assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the King of Jin took the imperial throne, declared a general amnesty, and inaugurated a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，奉魏帝爲陳留王，卽宮於鄴；

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the former Wei emperor was installed as Prince of Chenliu and took up residence at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the former Wei emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu and established his palace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 優崇之禮，皆仿魏初故事。

translations.literal: The honors and courtesies shown him all followed the precedents of early Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesies accorded him followed the precedents set when Wei had first received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 魏氏諸王皆降爲候。

translations.literal: All princes of the Wei house were demoted to marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Every prince of the Wei imperial clan was reduced in rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 追尊宣王爲宣皇帝，景王爲景皇帝，文王爲文皇帝。

translations.literal: King Xuan was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan, King Jing as Emperor Jing, and King Wen as Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan was posthumously elevated to Emperor Xuan, King Jing to Emperor Jing, and King Wen to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 尊王太后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The king's empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The king's mother was elevated to grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 封皇叔祖父孚爲安平王，叔父干爲平原王、亮爲扶風王、胄爲東莞王、駿爲汝陰王、肜爲梁王、倫爲琅邪王，弟攸爲齊王、鑒爲樂安王、機爲燕王，又封群從司徒望等十七人皆爲王。

translations.literal: The emperor's grand-uncle Fu was enfeoffed as Prince of Anping; his uncles Gan as Prince of Pingyuan, Liang as Prince of Fufeng, Zhou as Prince of Dongguan, Jun as Prince of Ruyin, Rong as Prince of Liang, and Lun as Prince of Langye; his brothers You as Prince of Qi, Jian as Prince of Le'an, and Ji as Prince of Yan; and seventeen collateral kinsmen including Minister over the Masses Wang were all enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his grand-uncle Fu as Prince of Anping; his uncles Gan, Liang, Zhou, Jun, Rong, and Lun as princes of Pingyuan, Fufeng, Dongguan, Ruyin, Liang, and Langye respectively; his brothers You, Jian, and Ji as princes of Qi, Le'an, and Yan; and seventeen collateral relatives, including Sima Wang, all received princely titles.

sentences.zh: 以石苞爲大司馬，鄭沖爲太傅，王祥爲太保，何曾爲太尉，賈充爲車騎將軍，王沈爲驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Shi Bao was appointed Grand Marshal, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, He Zeng Grand Commandant, Jia Chong General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Wang Shen Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao became Grand Marshal, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, He Zeng Grand Commandant, Jia Chong General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Wang Shen Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 其餘文武增位進爵有差。

translations.literal: The remaining civil and military officials received promotions of rank and title in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Other civil and military officials received promotions in rank and title according to their stations.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以安平王孚爲太宰，都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Prince of Anping Fu was appointed Grand Preceptor and put in overall command of all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Prince of Anping Fu was named Grand Preceptor with overall command of all military forces.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又以車騎將軍陳騫爲大將軍，與司徒義陽王望、司空荀顗，凡八公，同時並置。

translations.literal: Before long, General of Chariots and Cavalry Chen Qian was also appointed Grand General; together with Minister over the Masses Prince of Yiyang Wang and Minister of Works Xun Yi, eight grandees were all established at once.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chen Qian, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Grand General as well; with Minister over the Masses Prince of Yiyang Wang and Minister of Works Xun Yi, eight grand offices were filled simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 帝懲魏氏孤立之敝，故大封宗室，授以職任，又招諸王皆得自選國中長吏；

translations.literal: The emperor, taking warning from the Wei house's weakness through isolation, therefore enfeoffed the imperial clan on a grand scale, invested them with duties, and furthermore summoned all princes to select their own chief officials within their states.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of how the Wei house had been weakened by keeping its princes isolated, the emperor enfeoffed the imperial clan broadly, gave them real responsibilities, and allowed each prince to choose his own senior officials within his fief.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍齊王攸獨不敢，皆令上請。

translations.literal: Guard General Prince of Qi You alone did not dare to do so and had all appointments submitted for imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guard General Prince of Qi You declined to act on his own and referred every appointment to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔除魏宗室禁錮，罷部曲將及長吏納質任。

translations.literal: An edict removed the confinement imposed on the Wei imperial clan and abolished the requirement that commanders of military households and chief officials send hostages.
translations.idiomatic: An edict lifted the restrictions on Wei imperial clansmen and ended the practice of requiring military commanders and chief officials to post hostages at court.

sentences.zh: 帝承魏氏刻薄奢侈之後，欲矯以仁儉，太常丞許奇，允之子也，帝將有事於太廟，朝議以奇父受誅，不宜接近左右，請出爲外官；

translations.literal: The emperor, succeeding the harsh and extravagant ways of Wei, wished to correct them through benevolence and frugality. Xu Qi, son of Xu Yun, was a aide in the Ministry of Rites; when the emperor was about to perform rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, court opinion held that because Qi's father had been executed, he ought not approach the sovereign's person and requested that he be sent out as an external official.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to power after Wei's harsh extravagance, the emperor sought to correct it with benevolence and thrift. Xu Qi, son of the executed Xu Yun, served as an aide in the Ministry of Rites. When the emperor was to worship at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, court opinion argued that a son of a condemned man should not attend the sovereign and asked that Qi be posted outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝乃追述允之夙望，稱奇之才，擢爲祠部郎。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon recalled Yun's long-standing reputation, praised Qi's talent, and promoted him to Gentleman of the Sacrificial Department.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instead recalled Xu Yun's former standing, praised Qi's ability, and promoted him to Gentleman of the Sacrificial Department.

sentences.zh: 有司言御牛靑絲紖斷，詔以靑麻代之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported that the green silk reins of the imperial oxen had broken, and an edict ordered that green hemp be used in their place.
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported that the green silk reins on the imperial oxen had broken, an edict substituted green hemp instead.

sentences.zh: 初置諫官，以散騎常侍傅玄、皇甫陶爲之。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials were established for the first time, with Regular Attendant Fu Xuan and Huangfu Tao appointed to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time remonstrating officials were instituted, with Regular Attendant Fu Xuan and Huangfu Tao named to the office.

sentences.zh: 玄，干之子也。

translations.literal: Xuan was the son of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan was a son of Fu Gan.

sentences.zh: 玄以魏末士風頽敝，上疎曰：「臣聞先王之御天下，教化隆於上，淸議行於下。

translations.literal: Because scholarly mores at the end of Wei had collapsed, Xuan submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that when the former kings governed the realm, moral transformation flourished above and pure discourse prevailed below.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how debased scholarly conduct had become by the end of Wei, Xuan submitted a memorial: "I have heard that when the ancient kings ruled the realm, moral teaching flourished at court and upright discourse prevailed among the people.

sentences.zh: 近者魏武好法術而天下貴刑名，魏文慕通達而天下賤守節，其後綱維不攝，放誕盈朝，遂使天下無復淸議。

translations.literal: Recently Wei Wu favored legalism and the realm prized penal names; Wei Wen admired free-ranging talent and the realm despised holding to principle. Afterward the bonds of order were not maintained, unrestrained conduct filled the court, and thus the realm no longer had pure discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Wei Wu favored legal craft and the empire valued harsh penal administration; Wei Wen admired broad-minded talent and the empire scorned steadfast integrity. Thereafter the fabric of order unraveled, license filled the court, and pure discourse vanished from the land.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興受禪，弘堯、舜之化，惟未舉淸遠有禮之臣以敦風節，未退虚鄙之士以懲不恪，臣是以猶敢有言。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has risen like a dragon and received the abdication, spreading the transformation of Yao and Shun, yet you have not yet elevated pure, distant, and courteous ministers to strengthen moral conduct, nor dismissed empty and base scholars to punish lack of reverence; therefore I still dare to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ascended and received the mandate, spreading a Yao-and-Shun transformation, yet you have not yet promoted pure, principled ministers to strengthen public morals, nor removed shallow and unworthy men to punish irreverence—hence I still venture to speak."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納其言，使玄草詔進之，然亦不能革也。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted his words, had Xuan draft an edict to promote such men, yet still could not reform the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his advice, had Xuan draft an edict to advance worthy men, yet still could not change the times.

sentences.zh: 初，漢征西將軍司馬鈞生豫章太守量，量生穎川太守俊，俊生京兆尹防，防生宣帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han General Who Conquers the West Sima Jun begot Administrator of Yuzhang Liang; Liang begot Administrator of Yingchuan Jun; Jun begot Intendant of Jingzhao Fang; Fang begot Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han General Who Conquers the West Sima Jun fathered Yuzhang administrator Liang; Liang fathered Yingchuan administrator Jun; Jun fathered Jingzhao intendant Fang; and Fang fathered Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥，卽用魏廟祭征西府君以下並景帝凡七室。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day dinghai, the Wei ancestral temple was used to sacrifice to the Lord of the Western Expeditionary Headquarters and below, together with Emperor Jing—seven chambers in all.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dinghai, the court worshipped at the Wei ancestral temple, offering to the Western Expeditionary forebear and the succeeding generations through Emperor Jing—seven chambers in all.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，尊景帝夫人羊氏曰景皇后，居弘訓宮。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the consort of Emperor Jing, Lady Yang, was honored as Jing empress and took residence in Hongxun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Emperor Jing's consort, Lady Yang of the Yang clan, was elevated to Jing empress and installed in Hongxun Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙午，立皇后弘農楊氏。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Lady Yang of Hongnong was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Lady Yang of Hongnong was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 后，魏通事郎文宗之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the daughter of Wei Attendant for Miscellaneous Affairs Yang Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: She was a daughter of Yang Wenzong, Attendant for Miscellaneous Affairs under Wei.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏：「五帝卽天帝也，王氣時異，故名號有五。

translations.literal: The ministers submitted: "The Five Emperors are the Heavenly Emperor; as the royal qi differed with the times, their titles were five.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers submitted: "The Five Emperors are one with the Heavenly Emperor; only because the royal qi shifted with the ages did their titles number five.

sentences.zh: 自今明堂、南郊宜除五帝座。」

translations.literal: From now on, in the Bright Hall and at the Southern Suburb, the seats of the Five Emperors ought to be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the seats of the Five Emperors should be removed from the Bright Hall and the Southern Suburb rites."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 帝，王肅外孫也，故郊祀之禮，有司多從肅議。

translations.literal: The emperor was a maternal grandson of Wang Su, and therefore in suburban sacrifice rites the responsible offices mostly followed Su's views.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was Wang Su's maternal grandson, so in suburban sacrifice the responsible offices largely followed Su's opinions.

sentences.zh: 二月，除漢宗室禁錮。

translations.literal: In the second month, the confinement imposed on the Han imperial clan was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, restrictions on the Han imperial clan were lifted.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊戌，呉遣大鴻臚張儼、五官中郎將丁忠來弔祭。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuxu, Wu sent Grand Herald Zhang Yan and Palace Attendant of the Five Offices Ding Zhong to offer condolences and perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuxu, Wu dispatched Grand Herald Zhang Yan and Palace Attendant of the Five Offices Ding Zhong to offer mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 呉散騎常侍廬江王蕃，體氣髙亮，不能承顏順指，呉主不悅，散騎常侍萬彧、中書丞陳聲從而譖之。

translations.literal: Wu's Regular Attendant Wang Fan of Lujiang had a lofty and bright presence and could not comply with flattery and compliance; the Lord of Wu was displeased, and Regular Attendant Wan Yu and Secretariat Aide Chen Sheng slandered him in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan of Lujiang, Wu's Regular Attendant, was tall and forthright and would not flatter or yield; the Wu ruler disliked him, and Regular Attendant Wan Yu and Secretariat Aide Chen Sheng joined in slandering him.

sentences.zh: 丁忠使還，呉主大會群臣，蕃沉醉頓伏。

translations.literal: When Ding Zhong's mission returned, the Lord of Wu held a great assembly of the ministers; Fan, deeply drunk, collapsed prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Zhong's embassy returned, the Wu ruler held a grand feast for his ministers; Fan, dead drunk, slumped to the floor.

sentences.zh: 呉主疑其詐，輿蕃出外。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu suspected deception and had Fan carried out in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting a ruse, the ruler had Fan carried outside in a litter.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召還。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 蕃好治威儀，行止自若。

translations.literal: Fan was fond of maintaining dignified bearing, and his deportment remained as composed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, who prized dignified bearing, walked and stood as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 呉主大怒，呵左右於殿下斬之，出，登來山，使親近擲蕃首，作虎跳狼爭咋嚙之，首皆碎壞。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu was greatly enraged, shouted to his attendants to behead Fan below the hall steps, went out, ascended Mount Lai, and had his close followers throw Fan's head down; they acted out tigers leaping and wolves fighting, biting and gnawing it until the head was entirely shattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler flew into a rage, ordered his attendants to behead Fan on the hall steps, then climbed Mount Lai and had intimates cast down Fan's head while they mimicked tigers and wolves fighting, biting and tearing it until it was smashed to pieces.

sentences.zh: 丁忠説呉主曰：「北方無守戰之備，弋陽可襲而取。」

translations.literal: Ding Zhong urged the Lord of Wu, saying, "The north has no preparations for defense; Yiyang can be seized in a surprise attack."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Zhong urged the Wu ruler: "The north is unprepared for defense; Yiyang could be taken in a surprise strike."

sentences.zh: 呉主以問群臣，鎭西大將軍陸凱曰：「北方新並巴、蜀，遣使求和，非求援於我也，欲蓄力以俟時耳。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu asked the ministers; General Who Stabilizes the West Lu Kai said, "The north has newly annexed Ba and Shu, sent envoys seeking peace—not seeking aid from us, but wishing to store strength and await the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler consulted his ministers. Lu Kai, General Who Stabilizes the West, said: "The north has just absorbed Ba and Shu and sent envoys suing for peace—not because they need our help, but to husband their strength and wait for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 敵勢方強，而欲徼幸求勝，未見其利也。」

translations.literal: The enemy's strength is at its height, yet you wish to seek victory by chance—I do not see the advantage in this."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is at the height of his power, yet you would gamble on a lucky victory—I see no profit in that."

sentences.zh: 呉主雖不出兵，然遂與晉絶。

translations.literal: Although the Lord of Wu did not send out troops, he nevertheless broke relations with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Wu ruler sent no troops, he broke off relations with Jin.

sentences.zh: 凱，遜之族子也。

translations.literal: Kai was a clansman of Sun Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai was a kinsman of Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬子，博陵元公王沈卒。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, on the day renzi, Wang Shen, Duke Yuan of Boling, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on renzi, Wang Shen, Duke Yuan of Boling, died.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙午晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the last day of the cycle bingwu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the last day bingwu of the cycle, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 文帝之喪，臣民皆從權制，三日除服。

translations.literal: At the mourning for Emperor Wen, officials and people all followed expedient regulations and removed mourning garments after three days.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for Emperor Wen, officials and commoners alike followed expedient practice and laid aside mourning dress after three days.

sentences.zh: 旣葬，帝亦除之，然猶素冠疎食，哀毀如居喪者。

translations.literal: After the burial, the emperor also removed mourning dress, yet still wore a plain cap and ate sparingly, grieving and wasting away as one still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial the emperor too laid aside formal mourning, yet still wore a plain cap, ate sparingly, and grieved as though still in full mourning.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，帝將謁崇陽陵，群臣奏言，秋暑未平，恐帝悲感摧傷。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, the emperor was about to visit Chongyang Mausoleum; the ministers submitted that the autumn heat had not yet subsided and they feared grief might injure and weaken him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, as the emperor prepared to visit Chongyang Mausoleum, ministers urged that the late-summer heat had not yet broken and feared grief might overwhelm his health.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕得奉瞻山陵，體氣自佳耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When I can pay my respects at the mountain tomb, my bodily vigor will naturally improve."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Once I can pay my respects at the tomb, my health will improve of itself."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「漢文不使天下盡哀，亦帝王至謙之志。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict saying, "Emperor Wen of Han did not make the realm mourn fully—this too was the utmost humility of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed: "Emperor Wen of Han did not require the whole realm to mourn—that too was the utmost humility of a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 當見山陵，何心無服！

translations.literal: When I am to see the mountain tomb, how could my heart be without mourning dress!
translations.idiomatic: When I am about to visit the tomb, how could I go without mourning garb!

sentences.zh: 其議以衰絰從行。

translations.literal: Let it be discussed whether to wear hemp mourning and proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Let the court consider wearing hemp mourning for the journey.

sentences.zh: 群臣自依舊制。」

translations.literal: The ministers themselves followed the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers themselves adhered to the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 尚書令裴秀奏曰：「陛下旣除而復服，義無所依；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu submitted: "Your Majesty has already removed mourning yet puts it on again—there is no basis in ritual for this.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu submitted: "Your Majesty has already laid aside mourning yet would don it again—there is no ritual basis for that.

sentences.zh: 若君服而臣不服，亦未之敢安也。」

translations.literal: If the ruler wears mourning while his ministers do not, I also would not dare to be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign wears mourning while his ministers do not, we could scarcely feel at ease either."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「患情不能跂及耳，衣服何在！

translations.literal: An edict said, "I only fear that my feelings cannot reach that far—what does clothing matter!
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "I only fear my feelings cannot match the ritual—what does clothing matter!

sentences.zh: 諸君勤勤之至，豈苟相違。」

translations.literal: Your earnest diligence reaches so far—how could I casually oppose you?"
translations.idiomatic: Your earnest concern moves me deeply—how could I lightly oppose you?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He desisted.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍羊祜謂傅玄曰：「三年之喪，雖貴遂服，禮也，而漢文除之，毀禮傷義。

translations.literal: Central Army General Yang Hu said to Fu Xuan, "The three-year mourning, though even the noble complete it, is ritual; yet Emperor Wen of Han abolished it, destroying ritual and injuring righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army General Yang Hu said to Fu Xuan: "Three-year mourning is ritual—even nobles complete it—yet Emperor Wen of Han abolished it, damaging ritual and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今主上至孝，雖奪其服，實行喪禮。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign is supremely filial; though his mourning dress was taken away, in fact he is performing mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is deeply filial; though formal mourning was cut short, in practice he still observes mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 若因此復先王之法，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: If through this we restore the law of the former kings, would that not be good!"
translations.idiomatic: If we could use this occasion to restore the former kings' practice, would that not be excellent!"

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「以日易月，已數百年，一旦復古，難行也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said, "Replacing months with days has already lasted several hundred years; to restore antiquity all at once would be hard to carry out."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan replied: "Replacing months with days has stood for centuries; to restore the ancient practice overnight would be impracticable."

sentences.zh: 祜曰：「不能使天下如禮，且使主上遂服，不猶愈乎！」

translations.literal: Hu said, "If we cannot make the realm observe ritual, at least let the sovereign complete mourning dress—would that not be better!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said: "If we cannot make the whole realm observe ritual, at least let the sovereign complete full mourning—would that not be an improvement!"

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「主上不除而天下除之，此爲但有父子，無復君臣也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said, "If the sovereign does not remove mourning while the realm removes it, this means there are only father and son, and no longer ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: "If the sovereign keeps mourning while the realm lays it aside, we would have only the bond of father and son and no longer ruler and subject."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，群臣奏請易服復膳，詔曰：「毎感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰之禮，以爲沉痛。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the ministers submitted asking that he change garments and resume normal meals; an edict said, "Whenever I think of the departed in the nether world and cannot complete the hemp-mourning rites, I consider it a deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the ministers asked him to change dress and resume normal meals. An edict replied: "Whenever I think of my father in the nether world and cannot complete the full hemp mourning, the sorrow is overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 況當食稻衣錦乎！

translations.literal: How much less should I eat rice and wear brocade!
translations.idiomatic: How then could I eat rice and wear brocade!

sentences.zh: 適足激切其心，非所以相解也。

translations.literal: This would only sharpen and wound the heart—it is not the way to bring relief.
translations.idiomatic: That would only sharpen my grief, not ease it.

sentences.zh: 朕本諸生家，傳禮來久，何至一旦便易此情於所天！

translations.literal: I come originally from a scholar's household and have transmitted ritual for long—how could I in a single day change this feeling toward him who was as Heaven to me!
translations.idiomatic: I come from a scholar's family and have long upheld ritual—how could I change overnight this feeling for him who was my Heaven!

sentences.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也！」

translations.literal: You have already urged me at length; you might try reflecting on Confucius's reply to Zai Wo—there is no need for further clamor!"
translations.idiomatic: You have urged me long enough—consider Confucius's reply to Zai Wo, and trouble me no further!"

sentences.zh: 遂以疎素終三年。

translations.literal: He thereupon wore plain and simple dress to the end of the three years.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wore plain dress through the full three years.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：三年之喪，自天子達於庶人，此先王禮經，百世不易者也。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang remarks: The three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people—this is the ritual canon of the former kings, unchanging for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, is the ritual canon of the ancient kings—unchanged for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 漢文師心不學，變古壞禮，絶父子之恩，虧君臣之義；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han followed his own mind without learning, altered antiquity and ruined ritual, severed the grace between father and son, and diminished the righteousness between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han followed his own inclinations without studying ritual, altered antiquity and ruined ceremony, severed the bond between father and son, and weakened the bond between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 後世帝王不能篤於哀戚之情，而群臣諂諛，莫肯釐正。

translations.literal: Later generations of emperors could not be sincere in grief and sorrow, while the ministers flattered and fawned, none willing to correct the error.
translations.idiomatic: Later emperors could not sustain sincere mourning, while ministers flattered them and none would set matters right.

sentences.zh: 至於晉武獨以天性矯而行之，可謂不世之賢君；

translations.literal: As for Emperor Wu of Jin alone, by his natural disposition he corrected this and acted accordingly—he may be called an unmatched worthy ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin alone, by innate filial feeling, corrected the practice—he may be called a ruler of rare worth.

sentences.zh: 而裴、傅之徒，固陋庸臣，習常玩故，不能將順其美，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet Pei, Fu, and their kind were obstinate and mediocre ministers, accustomed to routine and playing with precedent, unable to follow and assist his excellence—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Pei Xiu, Fu Xuan, and men like them were narrow, mediocre officials, clinging to custom and precedent, unable to support his excellence—alas!

sentences.zh: 呉改元寶鼎。

translations.literal: Wu changed the era name to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu adopted Baoding as its new reign title.

sentences.zh: 呉主以陸凱爲左丞相，萬彧爲右丞相。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu appointed Lu Kai as Left Chancellor and Wan Yu as Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler appointed Lu Kai Left Chancellor and Wan Yu Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 呉主惡人視己，群臣侍見，莫敢舉目。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler hated people looking at him; when the ministers attended and saw him, none dared to raise their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor of Wu could not abide anyone's gaze upon him. When his ministers attended court, not one dared look up.

sentences.zh: 陸凱曰：「君臣無不相識之道，若猝有不虞，不知所赴。」

translations.literal: Lu Kai said, "Between sovereign and minister there is no proper way of not knowing one another; if something sudden and unforeseen should occur, one would not know where to turn."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai said, "Sovereign and subject ought to know one another. If disaster struck suddenly, how would Your Majesty know whom to trust?"

sentences.zh: 呉主乃聽凱自視，而它人如故。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler thereupon allowed Kai to look at him freely, but everyone else remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor relented only for Lu Kai, who might meet his eyes; all others were still forbidden to do so.

sentences.zh: 呉主居武昌，揚州之民溯流供給，甚苦之，又奢侈無度，公私窮匱。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler resided at Wuchang. The people of Yangzhou, going upstream to supply him, suffered greatly from it; moreover he was extravagant beyond measure, and both public and private coffers were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: With the Wu emperor lodged at Wuchang, the people of Yangzhou had to pole supplies upriver at grievous cost. His extravagance knew no bounds, and the treasury—public and private alike—was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 凱上疎曰：「今四邊無事，當務養民豐財，而更窮奢極欲，無災而民命盡，無爲而國財空，臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: Kai submitted a memorial saying, "Now that the four borders are at peace, we ought to nourish the people and enrich the state; yet instead we exhaust luxury and extreme desire. Without calamity the people's lives are spent; without achievement the state's wealth is emptied. Your servant is privately pained by this.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai memorialized the throne: "The frontiers are quiet; we should be nurturing the people and building up the treasury. Instead we pursue luxury to the limit. The people are being bled dry though no war rages; the state's wealth is squandered though no great task is accomplished. This grieves me deeply.

sentences.zh: 昔漢室旣衰，三家鼎立；

translations.literal: Formerly, when the Han house had already declined, three families stood in tripartite balance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty waned, three powers rose and divided the realm among themselves.

sentences.zh: 今曹、劉失道，皆爲晉有，此目前之明驗也。

translations.literal: Now Cao and Liu have lost the Way, and both have been taken by Jin. This is clear proof before our eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Today Cao Wei and Liu Shu have both lost the Mandate, and Jin has swallowed them both—a lesson plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 臣愚，但爲陛下惜國家耳。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish; I only grieve for Your Majesty's sake over the state.
translations.idiomatic: I speak as a plain man, Your Majesty, but my concern is for the survival of the realm itself.

sentences.zh: 武昌土地危險□脊確，非王者之都。

translations.literal: The land of Wuchang is perilous, barren and rugged; it is not a capital fit for a king.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang sits on treacherous, barren, rugged ground—it is no seat for an imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 且童謠云：『寧飲建業水，不食武昌魚；

translations.literal: Moreover a children's song says, "Better drink the water of Jianye than eat the fish of Wuchang;"
translations.idiomatic: Consider the children's rhyme: "We'd rather drink Jianye's water than eat Wuchang's fish—"

sentences.zh: 寧還建業死，不止武昌居。』

translations.literal: "Better return to Jianye to die than remain living at Wuchang."
translations.idiomatic: We'd rather die back in Jianye than go on living in Wuchang."

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，足明民心與天意矣。

translations.literal: Judging from this, it is enough to make clear the people's hearts and Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: From that alone one can read both the people's will and Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 今國無一年之蓄，民有離散之怨，國有露根之漸，而官吏務爲苛急，莫之或恤。

translations.literal: Now the state has not a year's store of grain; the people harbor resentment of being scattered and driven away; the state shows the first signs of roots laid bare to wither—and yet officials zealously pursue harsh urgency, and none show the least concern.
translations.idiomatic: The state lacks even a year's reserves. The people seethe with grievance and the realm shows the first signs of uprooting—yet officials compete in severity, and no one spares them a thought.

sentences.zh: 大帝時，後宮列女及諸織絡數不滿百，景帝以來，乃有千數，此耗財之甚者也。

translations.literal: In the time of the Great Emperor, the palace women and weaving attendants numbered less than a hundred; since Emperor Jing they have reached a thousand or more. This is an extreme drain on the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperor, palace women and weaving maids numbered fewer than a hundred. Since Emperor Jing's reign they have swelled to over a thousand—a ruinous drain on the treasury.

sentences.zh: 又左右之臣，率非其人，群黨相扶，害忠隱賢，此皆蠹政病民者也。

translations.literal: Moreover the ministers at Your Majesty's side are for the most part not the right men. Factions bolster one another, injure the loyal and conceal the worthy. All these are worms in government and sickness to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surround Your Majesty are, for the most part, unworthy men. Factions protect one another, strike down the loyal, and bury the able. Each of these is a canker on government and a plague upon the people.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下省息百役，罷去苛擾，料出宮女，淸選百官，則天悅民附，國家永安矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would reduce and cease the hundred corvées, abolish harsh disturbance, assess and release palace women, and cleanly select the hundred officials—then Heaven will be pleased, the people will attach themselves, and the state will be forever secure."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to cut back forced labor, end oppressive exactions, release surplus palace women, and appoint honest officials. Then Heaven will smile, the people will rally, and the state will endure."

sentences.zh: 呉主雖不悅，以其宿望，特優容之。

translations.literal: Although the Wu ruler was displeased, because of Kai's long-standing reputation he specially treated him with indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor took no pleasure in the admonition, but out of respect for Lu Kai's long service he let the rebuke pass without punishment.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔：「自今雖詔有所欲，及已奏得可，而於事不便者，皆不可隱情。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict said, "From now on, even if an edict expresses what is desired, and even if a memorial has already received approval, yet if the matter is inconvenient, none may conceal the facts."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict declared: "Henceforth, even when the throne has spoken its wish and a memorial has already won approval, if the matter is impracticable, no one may withhold the truth."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，有司奏：「大晉受禪於魏，宜一用前代正朔、服色，如虞遵唐故事。」

translations.literal: On the day wuxu the responsible officials memorialized, "Great Jin received the abdication from Wei; it is fitting to adopt uniformly the calendar and ceremonial colors of former dynasties, as Yu followed the precedent of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, the court memorialized: "Great Jin received the abdication from Wei. The dynasty ought to adopt the calendar and regalia of its predecessors, as Yu had followed the customs of Tang."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day of the cycle bingwu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the tenth month—the day bingwu—a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 永安山賊施但，因民勞怨，聚衆數千人，劫呉主庶弟永安侯謙作亂，北至建業，衆萬餘人，未至三十里住，擇吉日入城。

translations.literal: Shi Dan, a bandit of Yong'an Mountain, taking advantage of the people's labor and resentment, gathered several thousand men, seized the Wu ruler's younger brother by a concubine, the Marquis of Yong'an, Qian, and raised rebellion. Going north to Jianye, his force exceeded ten thousand men. When still thirty li short of the city they halted and chose an auspicious day to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan, a brigand of Mount Yong'an, exploited popular exhaustion and anger to rally several thousand followers. He seized the Wu emperor's younger half-brother, Marquis Qian of Yong'an, and rose in revolt. Marching on Jianye with more than ten thousand men, he halted thirty li from the city and waited for an auspicious day before entering.

sentences.zh: 遣使以謙命召丁固、諸葛靚，固、靚斬其使，發兵逆戰於牛屯。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger in Qian's name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing. Gu and Jing executed the messenger and raised troops to meet the enemy in battle at Niutun.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's rebels sent envoys in his name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing. The two men beheaded the messengers, mustered troops, and met the rebels in battle at Niutun.

sentences.zh: 但兵皆無甲冑，卽時敗散。

translations.literal: Dan's soldiers all lacked armor and helmets, and were immediately defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan's men wore no armor. They broke at once and fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 謙獨坐車中，生獲之。

translations.literal: Qian alone sat in his carriage and was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Qian alone remained seated in his carriage and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 固不敢殺，以狀白呉主，呉主並其母及弟俊皆殺之。

translations.literal: Gu did not dare to kill him and reported the facts to the Wu ruler. The Wu ruler executed Qian together with his mother and his brother Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gu dared not put him to death and reported the matter to the throne. The Wu emperor had Qian, his mother, and his brother Jun all executed.

sentences.zh: 初，望氣者云：「荊州有王氣，當破揚州。」

translations.literal: Earlier, readers of celestial omens had said, "Jing Province has kingly qi; it will overcome Yangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, omen-readers had declared, "Imperial destiny gathers in Jing Province; it will conquer Yangzhou."

sentences.zh: 故呉主徙都武昌。

translations.literal: For this reason the Wu ruler moved the capital to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On that account the Wu emperor had moved his capital to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 及但反，自以爲得計，遣數百人鼓噪入建業，殺但妻子，云「天子使荊州兵來破揚州賊。」

translations.literal: When Dan rebelled, the Wu ruler thought he had judged correctly. He sent several hundred men cheering and clamoring into Jianye, killed Dan's wife and children, and declared, "The Son of Heaven sent troops from Jing Province to destroy the rebels of Yangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dan rose, the Wu emperor convinced himself he had been right all along. He sent several hundred men into Jianye with drums and shouts, slaughtered Dan's wife and children, and proclaimed, "The Son of Heaven has sent Jingzhou troops to crush the Yangzhou rebels."

sentences.zh: 十一月，初並圜丘、方丘之祀於南北郊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, for the first time the sacrifices to the Round Mound and the Square Mound were combined at the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court for the first time combined the sacrifices to the Round Mound and the Square Mound, holding them at the southern and northern suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 罷山陽公國督軍，除其禁制。

translations.literal: The supervisory army over the State of the Duke of Shanyang was abolished, and his restrictions were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court abolished the garrison that had overseen the domain of the Duke of Shanyang and lifted the constraints placed upon him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，呉主還都建業，使后父衞將軍、録尚書事滕牧收留鎭武昌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Wu ruler returned the capital to Jianye and sent the empress's father, the Guard General and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Teng Mu, to remain and guard Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Wu emperor moved the capital back to Jianye and left the empress's father, Guard General Teng Mu—who also served as Recorder of the Masters of Writing—to hold Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 朝士以牧尊戚，頗推令諫爭，滕后之寵由是漸衰，更遣牧居蒼梧，雖爵位不奪，其實遷也，在道以憂死。

translations.literal: Because Mu was an honored relative by marriage, the court officials largely deferred to him in remonstrance. Empress Teng's favor thereby gradually declined. Mu was further sent to live in Cangwu. Though his rank was not stripped, in reality it was banishment; on the road he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Because Teng Mu was the emperor's father-in-law, court officials often yielded to him in debate—a fact that steadily eroded Empress Teng's standing. The emperor then sent Mu to live in exile at Cangwu. His title remained, but the move was banishment in all but name; he died of grief on the journey.

sentences.zh: 何太后常保佑滕后，太史又言中宮不可易。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager He constantly protected Empress Teng, and the Grand Astrologer also said the empress could not be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager He had always shielded Empress Teng, and the court astrologer declared that the empress could not be deposed.

sentences.zh: 呉主信巫覡，故得不廢，常供養昇平宮，不復進見，諸姬佩皇后璽紱者甚衆，滕后受朝賀表疎而已。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler trusted shamans and diviners, and so she was not deposed. She was constantly maintained at Shengping Palace and no longer received audiences. Many consorts wore the empress's seal and sash; Empress Teng merely received congratulatory memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor, a devout believer in shamans and diviners, kept Empress Teng on the throne but sequestered her at Shengping Palace, never granting her an audience again. A host of consorts wore the empress's seal and regalia, while Empress Teng herself received only the formal congratulatory memorials of state.

sentences.zh: 呉主使黃門遍行州郡，料取將吏家女，其二千石大臣子女，皆歳歳言名，年十五、六一簡閲，簡閲不中，乃得出嫁。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler sent palace attendants throughout the provinces and commanderies to assess and take the daughters of generals and officials. For daughters of ministers of two-thousand-bushel rank and above, their names were reported every year; at ages fifteen and sixteen they were inspected, and only if they failed inspection might they marry.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor dispatched palace eunuchs across every province and commandery to register and seize the daughters of officials and officers. Each year the names of daughters of ministers of two-thousand-bushel rank and above were submitted; at fifteen and sixteen they were examined, and only those rejected in the selection were permitted to marry.

sentences.zh: 後宮以千數，而采擇無已。

translations.literal: The palace women numbered in the thousands, yet the selection never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace already held a thousand women, yet the conscription of new ones never stopped.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁卯，立子衷爲皇太子。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day dingmao, the emperor's son Ai was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the dingmao day of the first month, Emperor Wu's son Ai was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 詔以「近世毎立太子必有赦，今世運將平，當示之以好惡，使百姓絶多幸之望。

translations.literal: An edict said, "In recent times, whenever a crown prince was established there was always an amnesty. The age's fortune is about to be settled; we ought to show the people good and evil, and make the common people abandon hopes of undeserved luck.
translations.idiomatic: An edict explained: "In recent generations the installation of a crown prince has always been marked by a general amnesty. Our age is nearing peace; the throne must teach the people to distinguish reward from punishment, and quench their appetite for undeserved fortune.

sentences.zh: 曲惠小人，朕無取焉！」

translations.literal: To show partial favor to petty men—I want none of it!"
translations.idiomatic: I will not indulge petty men with empty grace!"

sentences.zh: 遂不赦。

translations.literal: Thereupon no amnesty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: No amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉上黨李喜劾奏故立進令劉友、前尚書山濤、中山王睦、尚書僕射武陔各佔官稻田，請免濤、睦等官，陔已亡，請貶其諡。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing of Shangdang, Li Xi, impeached and memorialized that the former Director of Advancement Liu You, the former Master of Writing Shan Tao, the Prince of Zhongshan Mu, and the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wu Gai had each occupied official rice fields. He requested that Tao, Mu, and the others be removed from office; Gai was already dead, and he requested that his posthumous title be degraded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, Director of the Masters of Writing for Shangdang, impeached the former Director of Advancement Liu You, former Master of Writing Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, and Vice Director Wu Gai for seizing official rice fields. He asked that Tao, Mu, and the others be dismissed; Gai being already dead, he asked that his posthumous name be stripped.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「友侵剝百姓以謬惑朝士，其考竟以懲邪佞。

translations.literal: An edict said, "You exploited and stripped the people to deceive and bewilder court officials; let him be examined to the utmost to punish wicked flattery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Liu You squeezed the people and misled the court—let him be tried to the full extent of the law, as a warning to sycophants.

sentences.zh: 濤等不貳其過，皆勿有所問。

translations.literal: Tao and the others did not repeat their offense; let none of them be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao and the rest have not repeated their offense; let the matter against them drop.

sentences.zh: 喜亢志在公，當官而行，可謂邦之司直矣。

translations.literal: Xi, lofty in public spirit, acting in office as duty required, may be called the state's upright judge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi has served the public with fierce integrity and done his duty without flinching. He may truly be called the state's upright censor.

sentences.zh: 光武有云：『貴戚且斂手以避二鮑。』

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu once said, "Even the imperial kin must draw in their hands to avoid the two Baos."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu said, 'Even nobles must keep their hands to themselves lest they cross the two Baos.

sentences.zh: 其申敕群寮，各愼所詞，寬宥之恩，不可數遇也！」

translations.literal: Let this be announced and enjoined upon the whole body of officials; each should be careful in what he impeaches. The grace of broad pardon must not be granted again and again!"
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed to the whole bureaucracy: weigh your accusations carefully. The throne's mercy must not be squandered again and again!"

sentences.zh: 睦，宣帝之弟子也。

translations.literal: Mu was a younger cousin of Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu of Zhongshan was a younger cousin of Emperor Xuan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：政之大本，在於刑賞，刑賞不明，政何以成！

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The great foundation of government lies in punishments and rewards. If punishments and rewards are not clear, how can government be accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: The bedrock of government is reward and punishment. When reward and punishment are muddled, good governance is impossible.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝赦山濤而褒李喜，其於刑、賞兩失之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin pardoned Shan Tao and yet praised Li Xi; in punishments and rewards he erred on both counts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin pardoned Shan Tao even as he praised Li Xi—thus failing in both punishment and reward.

sentences.zh: 使喜所言爲是，則濤不可赦；

translations.literal: If what Xi said was correct, then Tao ought not to have been pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Li Xi's charges were true, Shan Tao should not have been spared.

sentences.zh: 所言爲非，則喜不足褒。

translations.literal: If what he said was incorrect, then Xi was not worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: If they were false, Li Xi deserved no praise.

sentences.zh: 褒之使言，言而不用，怨結於下，威玩於上，將安用之！

translations.literal: To praise him so that he speaks, yet not use what he says—resentment will bind those below, and authority will be played with above. Of what use is that!
translations.idiomatic: To praise a man into speaking truth, then ignore what he says, is to breed resentment below and make a mockery of authority above. What good can come of that?

sentences.zh: 且四臣同罪，劉友伏誅而濤等不問，避貴施賤，可謂政乎！

translations.literal: Moreover the four ministers shared the same crime: Liu You submitted to execution, yet Tao and the others were not questioned. To avoid the noble and apply punishment to the lowly—can this be called government!
translations.idiomatic: Worse, four men stood accused of the same crime: Liu You was put to death, while Shan Tao and the others went untouched. Spare the great, punish the small—is that governance?

sentences.zh: 創業之初，而政本不立，將以垂統後世，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: At the very beginning of founding the dynasty, if the foundation of government is not established, to intend thereby to hand down a model to later generations—is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: If the foundations of rule are not laid at the founding of a dynasty, what hope is there of bequeathing a worthy example to posterity?

sentences.zh: 帝以李喜爲太子太傅，徽犍爲李密爲洗馬。

translations.literal: The emperor made Li Xi Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and summoned Li Mi to serve as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Li Xi Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and summoned Li Mi to serve as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 密以祖母老，固辭，許之。

translations.literal: Mi, because his grandmother was old, firmly declined, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi declined on the grounds that his grandmother was aged and required his care. The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 密與人交，毎公議其得失而切責之，常言：「吾獨立於世，顧影無儔；

translations.literal: When Mi associated with others, he always openly discussed their right and wrong and sharply reproved them. He often said, "I stand alone in the world; looking at my shadow, I have no peer;
translations.idiomatic: In company Li Mi would openly weigh others' merits and faults and rebuke them without mercy. He was fond of saying, "I stand alone in this world. Look at my shadow—there is no one like me.

sentences.zh: 然而不懼者，以無彼此於人故也。」

translations.literal: yet the reason I am not afraid is that I make no distinction of self and other toward people."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear nothing, for I hold no private grudge against any man."

sentences.zh: 呉大赦，以右丞相萬彧鎭巴丘。

translations.literal: Wu granted a general amnesty and sent the Right Chancellor Wan Yu to guard Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu declared a general amnesty and posted Right Chancellor Wan Yu to guard Baling.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，呉主作昭明宮，二千石以下，皆自入山督伐木。

translations.literal: In summer, in the sixth month, the Wu ruler built the Zhaoming Palace. All officials of two-thousand-bushel rank and below went in person into the mountains to supervise the felling of timber.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, the Wu emperor began the Zhaoming Palace. Every official below two-thousand-bushel rank was sent personally into the hills to oversee the logging.

sentences.zh: 大開苑囿，起土山、樓觀，窮極伎巧，功役之費以億萬計。

translations.literal: He greatly opened parks and preserves, raised earthen hills and towered pavilions, exhausting every artifice of skill. The cost in labor and materials ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the imperial parks, raised artificial hills and lofty pavilions, and pushed craftsmanship to its utmost limit. The cost in labor and treasure ran into the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 陸凱諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Lu Kai remonstrated, but the Wu ruler would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai remonstrated. The emperor refused to hear him.

sentences.zh: 中書丞華覈上疎曰：「漢文之世，九州晏然，賈誼獨以爲如抱火厝於積薪之下而寢其上。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretary Hua He submitted a memorial saying, "In the age of Emperor Wen of Han the Nine Provinces were tranquil, yet Jia Yi alone thought it was like embracing fire and placing it beneath piled kindling while sleeping on top.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Hua He memorialized: "In Emperor Wen's reign the realm was at peace, yet Jia Yi warned that the dynasty slept atop a pile of kindling with a fire tucked beneath.

sentences.zh: 今大敵據九州之地，有太半之衆，欲與國家爲相呑之計，非徒漢之淮南、濟北而已也，比於賈誼之世，孰爲緩急？

translations.literal: Now the great enemy occupies the lands of the Nine Provinces and possesses more than half the population, intending a plan of mutual swallowing with our state. This is not merely Han's Huainan and Jibei. Compared with Jia Yi's age, which is urgent and which is relaxed?
translations.idiomatic: Today our great enemy holds most of the Nine Provinces and more than half the empire's people, and aims to devour us whole. This is no mere Huainan or Jibei rebellion. Compared with Jia Yi's day, which age faces the graver peril?

sentences.zh: 今倉庫空匱，編戸失業；

translations.literal: Now the storehouses are empty and depleted, and registered households have lost their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Our granaries stand empty; registered households have lost their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 而北方積穀養民，專心向東。

translations.literal: Yet in the north they accumulate grain and nourish the people, concentrating their hearts toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the north hoards grain, feeds its people, and turns every mind toward conquest of the east.

sentences.zh: 又，交趾淪沒，嶺表動搖，胸背有嫌，首尾多難，乃國朝之厄會也。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiaozhi has fallen, the region beyond the ranges is shaken, there is trouble front and back and difficulty at head and tail. This is a crisis moment for our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi has fallen; the Lingnan frontier trembles. We are threatened at our back even as our front buckles—a crisis on every front for our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 若捨此急務，盡力功作，卒有風塵不虞之變，當委版築而應烽燧，驅怨民而赴白刃，此乃大敵所因以爲資者也。」

translations.literal: If we abandon this urgent business and exhaust our strength on construction works, then when suddenly there is unforeseen turmoil from war, we must throw down trowel and board to answer beacon fires, and drive resentful people toward naked blades. This is precisely the resource our great enemy will rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: If we neglect these urgencies and pour all our strength into building, then when war erupts without warning we must drop our tools to answer the beacon fires and drive a resentful populace against naked steel. That is exactly the opening our enemy waits for."

sentences.zh: 時呉俗奢侈，覈又上疎曰：「今事多而役繁，民貧而俗奢，百工作無用之器，婦人爲綺靡之飾，轉相倣傚，恥獨無有。

translations.literal: At that time Wu's customs were extravagant. He again submitted a memorial saying, "Now affairs are many and corvées heavy; the people are poor yet customs are luxurious. The hundred craftsmen make useless vessels; women make ornate and extravagant adornments. They copy one another in turn and are ashamed to be the only ones without such things.
translations.idiomatic: Wu society had grown extravagantly wasteful. Hua He memorialized again: "Affairs multiply and corvée labor grows heavier, yet the people grow poorer while fashion grows more lavish. Craftsmen fashion useless gewgaws; women weave finery beyond all need. Each imitates the next, ashamed to be left out.

sentences.zh: 兵民之家，猶復逐俗，内無甔石之儲而出有綾綺之服，上無尊卑等級之差，下有耗財費力之損，求其富給，庸可得乎？」

translations.literal: Even in households of soldiers and common people they still follow the fashion: within they have not a stone's store of grain, yet outwardly they wear silk and brocade; above there is no distinction of high and low in rank, below there is loss of wealth and waste of strength. To seek riches and sufficiency—how can it be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: Even soldiers' and commoners' households chase the fashion: no grain in the jar, yet silk on their backs; no respect for rank above, ruinous expense below. Under such conditions, how can anyone prosper?"

sentences.zh: 呉主皆不聽。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler would not listen to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，王祥以睢陵公罷。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wang Xiang was dismissed from his post as Duke of Suiling.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Xiang was removed from his post as Duke of Suiling.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲申，詔增吏俸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jiashen, an edict increased officials' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day jiashen, an edict raised official salaries.

sentences.zh: 以何曾爲太保，義陽王望爲太尉，荀顗爲司徒。

translations.literal: He made He Zeng Grand Guardian, the Prince of Yiyang Wang Grand Commandant, and Xun Xu Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng was appointed Grand Guardian, Prince Wang of Yiyang Grand Commandant, and Xun Xu Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 禁星氣、讖緯之學。

translations.literal: The study of star qi and apocryphal prognostications was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The court forbade the study of celestial portents and apocryphal prophecy.

sentences.zh: 呉主以孟仁守丞相，奉法駕東迎其父文帝神於明陵，中使相繼，奉問起居。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler made Meng Ren acting chancellor, and with the imperial carriage went east to welcome the spirit of his father Emperor Wen from Ming Tomb. Palace envoys followed one after another, presenting inquiries after his well-being.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor appointed Meng Ren acting chancellor and rode the imperial carriage east to welcome his father Emperor Wen's spirit from Ming Tomb, while palace envoys followed in succession to inquire after the departed emperor's repose.

sentences.zh: 巫覡言見文帝被服顏色如平生。

translations.literal: Shamans and diviners said they saw Emperor Wen's dress and complexion as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans and diviners claimed to see Emperor Wen dressed and complected exactly as in life.

sentences.zh: 呉主悲喜，迎拜於東門之外。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler, both grieved and joyful, went out to welcome and bow at the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor, torn between grief and joy, went out to the east gate to receive the spirit and bow in homage.

sentences.zh: 旣入廟，比七日三祭，設諸倡伎，晝夜娯樂。

translations.literal: After it had entered the temple, for seven days there were three offerings, with every sort of performer and musician; day and night they amused themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Once the spirit entered the temple, the court held three sacrifices over seven days, with singers, dancers, and musicians performing day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 是歳，遣鮮卑拓跋沙漠汗歸其國。

translations.literal: That year the Xianbei Tuo Ba Shamo Han was sent back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court sent the Xianbei chieftain Tuoba Shamo Han home to his people.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙戌，賈充等上所刊修律令。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day bingxu, Jia Chong and others submitted the revised code of laws and ordinances to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the bingxu day of the first month, Jia Chong and his colleagues presented the newly compiled code of laws to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝親自臨講，使尚書郎裴楷執讀。

translations.literal: The emperor personally attended the exposition and had the Masters of Writing Attendant Pei Kai read it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor presided over the reading in person and had Masters of Writing Attendant Pei Kai recite the text.

sentences.zh: 楷，秀之從弟也。

translations.literal: Kai was a younger cousin of Pei Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai was the younger cousin of Pei Xiu.

sentences.zh: 侍中盧珽、中書侍郎范陽張華請抄新律死罪條目，懸之亭傳以示民，從之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Lu Zhi and the Palace Secretary of Fanyang, Zhang Hua, requested that the articles on capital crimes in the new code be copied out and posted at relay stations to show the people. The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Lu Zhi and Palace Secretary Zhang Hua of Fanyang asked that the capital-crime articles of the new code be copied and posted at relay stations for the people to see. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又詔河南尹杜預爲黜陟之課，預奏：「古者黜陟，擬議於心，不泥於法；

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Intendant of Henan Du Yu to draft regulations for promotion and dismissal. Yu memorialized, "In antiquity promotion and dismissal were deliberated in the heart and not bound to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also charged Intendant of Henan Du Yu with drafting rules for the evaluation and promotion of officials. Du Yu memorialized: "In antiquity, promotion and dismissal were weighed in the ruler's judgment, not shackled to written law.

sentences.zh: 末世不能紀遠而專求密微，疑心而信耳目，疑耳目而信簡書。

translations.literal: In decadent ages one cannot keep distant principles in view and instead seeks only minute detail; one distrusts the heart and trusts the ears and eyes; one distrusts the ears and eyes and trusts written documents.
translations.idiomatic: Decadent ages cannot grasp principle from afar and so chase microscopic detail; they distrust judgment and trust what the eyes and ears report; they distrust even the eyes and ears and trust only what is written down.

sentences.zh: 簡書愈繁，官方愈偽。

translations.literal: The more numerous the written documents, the more false officials become.
translations.idiomatic: The more paperwork proliferates, the more officials turn to artifice.

sentences.zh: 魏氏考課，卽京房之遺意，其文可謂至密，然失於苛細以違本體，故歴代不能通也。

translations.literal: The Wei dynasty's examination of performance was the legacy of Jing Fang's intent; its text may be called extremely detailed, yet it failed through harsh minuteness that violated the root substance, and so it could not be applied through successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's performance-examination system preserved Jing Fang's design. Its regulations were exhaustively detailed, yet so finicky that they betrayed the system's purpose—and no dynasty since has been able to make them work.

sentences.zh: 豈若申唐堯之舊制，取大捨小，去密就簡，俾之易從也！

translations.literal: How much better to restore the old system of Tang Yao, taking the large and abandoning the small, leaving the dense and seeking the simple, and making it easy to follow!
translations.idiomatic: Better to restore the ancient practice of Emperor Yao of Tang: keep what matters, discard the trivial; favor simplicity over complexity; make the law easy to obey.

sentences.zh: 夫曲盡物理，神而明之，存乎其人；

translations.literal: To exhaust the principles of things to the utmost, to divine and clarify them, depends on the man.
translations.idiomatic: To grasp affairs fully and judge them with insight depends on the person who wields authority.

sentences.zh: 去人而任法，則以文傷理。

translations.literal: To remove the man and rely on law is to let the letter injure principle.
translations.idiomatic: Remove the person and rely on the text alone, and the letter of the law will kill its spirit.

sentences.zh: 莫若委任達官，各考所統，歳第其人，言其優劣。

translations.literal: Better to entrust high officials, have each examine those under his command, rank the men year by year, and speak of their excellence or inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Better to entrust senior officials to evaluate their own subordinates, rank them annually, and report their strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 如此六載，主者總集，采案其言，六優者超擢，六劣者廢免，優多劣少者平敘，劣多優少者左遷。

translations.literal: In this way, after six years the responsible superior would gather the reports, examine the testimony, promote those with six counts of excellence, dismiss those with six counts of inferiority, give ordinary advancement to those with more excellence than inferiority, and demote those with more inferiority than excellence.
translations.idiomatic: After six years the supervising minister would compile the records: six years rated superior—promote; six rated inferior—dismiss; more superior than inferior—advance in regular course; more inferior than superior—demote.

sentences.zh: 其間所對不鈞，品有難易，主者固當准量輕重，微加降殺，不足曲以法盡也。

translations.literal: Where the responses within that period were uneven and the grades had easy and difficult points, the responsible superior should properly weigh light and heavy and slightly reduce or lessen the outcome; it is not enough to exhaust every turn through law.
translations.idiomatic: Where ratings varied or posts differed in difficulty, the supervising minister should weigh circumstances and adjust accordingly—not force every case through rigid formulae.

sentences.zh: 其有優劣徇情，不叶公論者，當委監司隨而彈之。

translations.literal: Where there was excellence or inferiority swayed by private feeling and not in accord with public judgment, the supervising censor should be entrusted to impeach according to the case.
translations.idiomatic: Where favoritism skewed the ratings against public opinion, the censorate should investigate and impeach.

sentences.zh: 若令上下公相容過，此爲淸議大頽，雖有考課之法，亦無益也。」

translations.literal: If one ordered those above and below publicly to cover one another's faults, this would be a great collapse of pure judgment; even if there were a method of examination, it would be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: If superiors and subordinates are allowed to shield one another's failings, honest judgment collapses—and no examination system, however elaborate, will do any good."

sentences.zh: 事竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝耕籍田於洛水之北。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, the emperor plowed the ceremonial field north of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the emperor performed the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field north of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 戊子，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，呉主以左御史大夫丁固爲司徒，右御史大夫孟仁爲司空。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Lord of Wu appointed Left Imperial Censor Grandee Ding Gu as Minister over the Masses and Right Imperial Censor Grandee Meng Ren as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Wu ruler made Left Imperial Censor Grandee Ding Gu Minister over the Masses and Right Imperial Censor Grandee Meng Ren Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊子，皇太后王氏殂。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuzi, the empress dowager, Lady Wang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuzi, Empress Dowager Wang died.

sentences.zh: 帝居喪之制，一遵古禮。

translations.literal: The emperor's mourning regulations followed the ancient rites in full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor observed mourning according to the full ancient ritual code.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊戌，睢陵元公王祥卒，門無雜吊之賓。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day xuxu, Duke Yuan of Suiling, Wang Xiang, died; at his gate there were no miscellaneous mourners.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on xuxu in the fourth month, Wang Xiang, Duke Yuan of Suiling, died; only proper mourners came to his gate.

sentences.zh: 其族孫戎歎曰：「太保當正始之世，不在能言之流；

translations.literal: His clansman Wang Rong sighed and said, "When the Grand Protector lived in the Zhengshi era, he was not counted among the eloquent speakers;
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Wang Rong remarked, "In the Zhengshi period the Grand Protector was not reckoned among the fluent talkers;

sentences.zh: 及間與之言，理致淸遠，豈非以德掩其言乎！」

translations.literal: yet when one spoke with him on occasion, his principles were clear and far-reaching—was it not that virtue overshadowed his words!"
translations.idiomatic: yet when you did speak with him, his reasoning was lucid and profound—surely virtue outshone mere eloquence!"

sentences.zh: 已亥，葬文明皇后。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, the Civilized Empress was buried.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the Civilized Empress was interred.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「旣虞，除衰服。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials again memorialized, "After the yu sacrifice, remove the mourning garments."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized again: "After the yu sacrifice, the mourning garments should be removed."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「受終身之愛而無數年之報，情所不忍也。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "To receive a lifetime's love and have no years of repayment—emotionally I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "She gave me a lifetime of devotion; to repay that in only a few years of mourning is more than my heart can bear."

sentences.zh: 有司固請，詔曰：「患在不能篤孝，勿以毀傷爲憂。

translations.literal: The officials pressed again; the edict said, "The worry is inability to be sincerely filial—do not grieve over self-injury.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed again, the emperor said: "My fear is that I cannot mourn sincerely enough—do not urge me to harm myself through excess.

sentences.zh: 前代禮典，質文不同，何必限以近制，使達喪闕然乎！」

translations.literal: The ritual classics of former ages differ in substance and ornament; why must we be bound by recent regulations and leave distant mourning incomplete?"
translations.idiomatic: Ancient ritual texts differ in substance and ornament; why bind ourselves to recent custom and leave the full term of mourning unfulfilled?"

sentences.zh: 群臣請不已，乃許之。

translations.literal: The ministers kept requesting without cease; he finally assented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers would not relent, and at last he consented.

sentences.zh: 然猶素冠疎食以終三年，如文帝之喪。

translations.literal: Yet he still wore a plain white cap and ate simple food to the end of three years, as in Emperor Wen's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He still wore undyed cap and plain food through the full three years, as Emperor Wen had done.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，衆星西流如雨而隕。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, many stars flowed westward like rain and fell.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, stars streamed westward like a shower and fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝謁崇陽陵。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the emperor visited Chongyang Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the emperor paid a visit to Chongyang Tomb.

sentences.zh: 九月，靑、徐、兗、豫四州大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the four provinces of Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu provinces were struck by severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 大司馬石苞久在淮南，威惠甚著。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Shi Bao had long been in Huainan; his prestige and kindness were very marked.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Shi Bao had long held Huainan, where his authority and benevolence were widely felt.

sentences.zh: 淮北監軍王琛惡之，密表苞與呉人交通。

translations.literal: Wang Chen, supervisory commander of north of the Huai, hated him and secretly memorialized that Bao was in communication with the Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, the north-of-Huai supervisory commander, detested him and secretly reported that Bao was trafficking with Wu.

sentences.zh: 會呉人將入寇，苞築壘遏水以自固，帝疑之。

translations.literal: When the Wu were about to invade, Bao built ramparts to block the water and secure himself; the emperor grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu forces threatened invasion, Bao built dikes to hold back the waters and fortify his position, and the emperor grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 羊祜深爲帝言苞必不然，帝不信，乃下詔以苞不料賊勢，築壘遏水，勞擾百姓，策免其官。

translations.literal: Yang Hu spoke earnestly to the emperor that Bao would certainly not do such a thing; the emperor did not believe it and issued an edict that Bao had misjudged the bandits' movements, built ramparts to block water, and troubled and harassed the people, and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu assured the emperor that Bao would never betray him, but the emperor would not listen. He issued an edict faulting Bao for misreading the enemy, wasting labor on dikes, and harassing the people, and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 遣義陽王望帥大軍以征之。

translations.literal: He sent the Prince of Yiyang, Wang, to lead a great army to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the Prince of Yiyang, Sima Wang, at the head of a large army to move against him.

sentences.zh: 苞辟河内孫鑠爲掾，鑠先與汝陰王駿善，駿時鎭許昌，鑠過見之。

translations.literal: Bao recruited Sun Shuo of Henei as his clerk; Shuo had earlier been on good terms with the Prince of Ru'nan, Jun, who was then stationed at Xuchang, and Shuo went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao took on Sun Shuo of Henei as an aide; Shuo was friendly with Prince Ru'nan Sima Jun, then posted at Xuchang, and went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 駿知台已遣軍襲苞，私告之曰：「無與於禍！」

translations.literal: Jun knew the throne had already sent troops to strike Bao and privately told him, "Have no part in the calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun knew the court had already dispatched troops against Bao and warned him privately: "Stay out of this disaster!"

sentences.zh: 鑠旣出，馳詣壽春，勸苞放兵，歩出都亭待罪，苞從之。

translations.literal: After Shuo left, he raced to Shouchun and urged Bao to dismiss his troops, walk out to the capital relay station, and await punishment; Bao followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo rode straight to Shouchun, urged Bao to disband his forces and present himself at the capital relay station to await judgment; Bao did so.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，意解。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, his resentment eased.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, his anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 苞詣闕，以樂陵公還第。

translations.literal: Bao came to the palace and returned home as Duke of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Bao appeared at court and was sent home with the title Duke of Leling.

sentences.zh: 呉主出東關，冬，十月，使其將施績入江夏，萬彧寇襄陽。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu went out through Dong Pass; in winter, in the tenth month, he sent his general Shi Ji into Jiangxia and Wan Yu to raid Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler marched out through Dong Pass; in winter, in the tenth month, he sent Shi Ji against Jiangxia and Wan Yu against Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 詔義陽王望統中軍歩騎二萬屯龍陂，爲二方聲援。
