translations.literal: An edict ordered the Prince of Yiyang, Wang, to command twenty thousand infantry and cavalry of the central army stationed at Long Slope as support for both fronts.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Prince Yiyang Sima Wang to hold Long Slope with twenty thousand central-army foot and horse as a reserve for both theaters.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史胡烈拒績，破之，望引兵還。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector Hu Lie resisted Ji and defeated him; Wang led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province inspector Hu Lie repelled Shi Ji and routed him; Sima Wang then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 呉交州刺史劉俊、大都督脩則、將軍顧容前後三攻交趾，交趾太守楊稷皆拒破之，鬱林、九眞皆附於稷。

translations.literal: Wu's Inspector of Jiaozhi, Liu Jun, Grand Coordinator Xiu Ze, and General Gu Rong attacked Jiaozhi three times in succession; Jiaozhi Governor Yang Ji repelled and defeated them each time, and Yulin and Jiuzhen both submitted to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's Jiaozhi inspector Liu Jun, grand coordinator Xiu Ze, and general Gu Rong attacked Jiaozhi three times running; governor Yang Ji beat them back each time, and Yulin and Jiuzhen submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 稷遣將軍毛炅、董元攻合浦，戰於古城，大破呉兵，殺劉俊、脩則，餘兵散還合浦。

translations.literal: Ji sent Generals Mao Jing and Dong Yuan to attack Hepu; they fought at Gucheng, inflicted a great defeat on Wu troops, killed Liu Jun and Xiu Ze, and the remaining soldiers scattered and returned to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent Mao Jing and Dong Yuan against Hepu; at Gucheng they crushed the Wu army, killed Liu Jun and Xiu Ze, and the survivors fled back to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 稷表炅爲鬱林太守，元爲九眞太守。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized that Jing be made Governor of Yulin and Yuan Governor of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ji recommended Mao Jing as governor of Yulin and Dong Yuan as governor of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 十一月，呉丁奉、諸葛靚出芍陂，攻合肥，安東將軍汝陰王駿拒卻之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wu's Ding Feng and Zhuge Liang came out through Shao Slope and attacked Hefei; Andong General the Prince of Ru'nan repelled and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wu generals Ding Feng and Zhuge Liang advanced from Shao Slope against Hefei; Andong general Prince Ru'nan beat them back.

sentences.zh: 以義陽王望爲大司馬，荀顗爲太尉，石苞爲司徒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yiyang, Wang, was made Grand Marshal; Xun Yi was made Grand Commandant; and Shi Bao was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wang was appointed Grand Marshal, Xun Yi Grand Commandant, and Shi Bao Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，呉主立子瑾爲皇太子。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, the Lord of Wu established his son Jin as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, the Wu ruler named his son Sun Jin crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二月，分雍、涼、梁州置秦州，以胡烈爲刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yong, Liang, and Liang Province were divided to establish Qin Province, with Hu Lie as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Qin Province was carved out of Yong, Liang, and Liang domains, with Hu Lie as its inspector.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄧艾納鮮卑降者數萬，置於雍、涼之間，與民雜居，朝廷恐其久而爲患，以烈素著名於西方，故使鎭撫之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Deng Ai had accepted several tens of thousands of surrendered Xianbei and settled them between Yong and Liang, mixed among the people; the court feared that in time this would become a trouble and, because Lie was renowned in the west, assigned him to pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Deng Ai had settled tens of thousands of surrendered Xianbei among the people of Yong and Liang; fearing future unrest, the court sent the celebrated western commander Hu Lie to keep them in order.

sentences.zh: 靑、徐、兗三州大水。

translations.literal: The three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces were ravaged by flooding.

sentences.zh: 帝有滅呉之志，壬寅，以尚書左僕射羊祜都督荊州諸軍事，鎭襄陽；

translations.literal: The emperor harbored the ambition to destroy Wu; on the day renchen he appointed Left Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Hu to supervise military affairs in Jing Province and station at Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Intent on conquering Wu, on renchen the emperor named Yang Hu, Left Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing, to command Jing Province from Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 征東大將軍衞瑾都督靑州諸軍事，鎭臨菑；

translations.literal: Eastern Campaign Grand General Wei Guan to supervise military affairs in Qing Province and station at Linzi;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Campaign grand general Wei Guan to hold Qing Province from Linzi;

sentences.zh: 鎭東大將軍東莞王人由都督徐州諸軍事，鎭下邳。

translations.literal: and Eastern Pacification Grand General the Prince of Dongguan to supervise military affairs in Xu Province and station at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: and Eastern Pacification grand general Prince Dongguan to hold Xu Province from Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 祜綏懷遠近，甚得江、漢之心。

translations.literal: Hu soothed those near and far and greatly won the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu won over neighbors and newcomers alike and gained deep loyalty throughout the middle Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 與呉人開布大信，降者欲去，皆聽之。

translations.literal: With the Wu he spread great trust; deserters who wished to leave were all permitted to go.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt openly with Wu and allowed defectors who wished to return to do so freely.

sentences.zh: 減戍邏之卒，以墾田八百餘頃。

translations.literal: He reduced border-guard soldiers and opened eight hundred-odd qing of reclaimed farmland.
translations.idiomatic: He cut garrison strength and brought more than eight hundred qing under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 其始至也，軍無百日之糧，及其季年，乃有十年之積。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, the army had not a hundred days' grain; by his final years there was a ten-year store.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the army had less than a hundred days' provisions; by the end of his tenure it held a ten-year reserve.

sentences.zh: 祜在軍，常輕裘緩帶，身不被甲，鈴閣之下，侍衞不過十數人。

translations.literal: When Hu was in the army he often wore a light fur robe with loose sash, his body unarmored; beneath the bell pavilion his attendants did not exceed a dozen or so.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he wore light robes and no armor; at headquarters his personal guard rarely numbered more than a dozen.

sentences.zh: 濟陰太守巴西文立上言：「故蜀之名臣子孫流徙中國者，宜量才敘用，以慰巴、蜀之心，傾呉人之望。」

translations.literal: Jiyin Governor Wen Li of Brazil submitted a memorial: "The descendants of famous ministers of former Shu, exiled in the Central States, should be appointed according to their talents to comfort the hearts of Ba and Shu and incline the hopes of the people of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin governor Wen Li of Brazil memorialized: "Former Shu ministers' descendants now living in the north should be placed according to ability—to reassure Ba-Shu loyalists and unsettle Wu's hopes."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔曰：「諸葛亮在蜀，盡其心力，其子瞻臨難而死義，其孫京宜隨才署吏。」

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, an edict said, "Zhuge Liang in Shu exhausted his heart and strength; his son Zhan met hardship and died in righteousness; his grandson Jing should be appointed to office according to his talent."
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an edict declared: "Zhuge Liang gave Shu his all; his son Zhan died loyal; his grandson Jing should receive office suited to his ability."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「蜀將傅僉父子死於其主。

translations.literal: Another edict said, "Shu general Fu Qian, father and son, died for their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "Shu general Fu Qian and his son died for their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 天下之善一也，豈由彼此以爲異哉！

translations.literal: Goodness under Heaven is one—how could one treat this and that as different!
translations.idiomatic: Virtue is one under Heaven—how can loyalty to one ruler differ from loyalty to another?

sentences.zh: 僉息著、募沒入奚官，宜免爲庶人。」

translations.literal: Qian's son Zhuo, conscripted into the palace service corps, should be exempted and made a commoner."
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Zhuo, impressed into palace service, should be freed and restored to commoner status."

sentences.zh: 帝以文立爲散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Wen Li as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Wen Li Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 漢故尚書犍爲程瓊，雅有德業，與立深交。

translations.literal: Former Han Masters of Writing Cheng Qiong of Jianwei was elegant in virtue and achievement and was on deep terms of friendship with Li.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han Masters of Writing Cheng Qiong of Jianwei, a man of sterling character, was Wen Li's close friend.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其名，以問立，對曰：「臣至知其人，但年垂八十，稟性謙退，無復當時之望，故不以上聞耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard his name and asked Li about him; Li replied, "I know the man well, but he is nearly eighty, his nature humble and retiring, and no longer has the hopes of that time—so I did not report him above."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Li about him; Li answered: "I know him well, but he is nearly eighty, modest by nature, and past the ambitions of youth—so I did not bring his name forward."

sentences.zh: 瓊聞之，曰：「廣休可謂不黨矣，此吾所以善夫人也。」

translations.literal: When Qiong heard of it he said, "Guangxiu can be called not partisan—this is why I befriend the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Qiong said: "Guangxiu is truly impartial—that is why I esteem him."

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，有星孛於紫宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the ninth month, a comet appeared in the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the ninth month, a comet blazed in the Purple Palace constellation.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，呉大赦，改元建衡。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Wu declared a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Jianheng.

sentences.zh: 封皇子景度爲城陽王。

translations.literal: Prince Jingdu was enfeoffed as Prince of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed Prince Jingdu as Prince of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 初，汝南何定嘗爲呉大帝給使，及呉主卽位，自表先帝舊人，求還内侍。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Ding of Runan had once served the Great Emperor of Wu as an attendant; when the Lord of Wu succeeded to the throne, Ding memorialized himself as an old man of the former emperor and sought to return to inner service.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Runan's He Ding had served Wu's founding emperor; when Sun Hao took the throne, Ding petitioned to return to palace service as a veteran of the old court.

sentences.zh: 呉主以爲樓下都尉，典知酤糴事，遂專爲威福；

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu made him Commandant of the Lower Pavilion, in charge of the sale of wine and grain, and he monopolized prestige and favors.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler made him Lower Pavilion commandant overseeing wine and grain sales, and he abused the post for private power.

sentences.zh: 呉主信任之，委以衆事。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu trusted him and entrusted him with many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler trusted him and handed him wide authority.

sentences.zh: 左丞相陸凱面責定曰：「卿見前後事主不忠，傾亂國政，寧有得以壽終者邪！

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Lu Kai reproached Ding to his face, saying, "You have seen service to former and later lords without loyalty, overturning and disordering state affairs—can there be anyone who ends his days in peace!
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Lu Kai confronted He Ding: "You have served successive rulers disloyally and wrecked the government—who ever died in bed after that?

sentences.zh: 何以專爲奸邪，塵穢天聽！

translations.literal: Why do you specialize in wickedness and defile the heavens' hearing!
translations.idiomatic: Why heap corruption on the throne's ears?

sentences.zh: 宜自改厲，不然，方見卿有不測之禍。」

translations.literal: You ought to reform yourself; otherwise you will soon see unforeseen disaster befall you."
translations.idiomatic: Reform—or you will meet disaster you cannot foresee."

sentences.zh: 定大恨之。

translations.literal: Ding hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Ding nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 凱竭心公家，忠懇内發，表疎皆指事不飾。

translations.literal: Kai devoted his heart to the public house; his loyalty was earnest within, and his memorials all pointed to matters without ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Kai served the state with tireless honesty; his memorials spoke plainly to the facts.

sentences.zh: 及疾病，呉主遣中書令董朝問所欲言，凱陳「何定不可信用，宜授以外任。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, the Lord of Wu sent Palace Secretary Dong Chao to ask what he wished to say; Kai stated, "He Ding cannot be trusted and should be given an outer assignment.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai fell ill, the Wu ruler sent Palace Secretary Dong Chao to ask his counsel; Kai said: "He Ding is not to be trusted—post him far from court.

sentences.zh: 奚熙小吏，建起浦里田，亦不可聽。

translations.literal: Xi Xi, a minor clerk, who built fields at the Puli lane, also cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk Xi Xi, who seized Puli lane for private fields, must be stopped.

sentences.zh: 姚信、樓玄、賀邵、張悌、郭逴、薛瑩、滕修及族弟喜、抗，或淸白忠勤，或資才卓茂，皆社稷之良輔，願陛下重留神思，訪以時務，使各盡其忠，拾遺萬一。」

translations.literal: Yao Xin, Lou Xuan, He Shao, Zhang Ti, Guo Chuo, Xue Ying, Teng Xiu, and his cousins Xi and Kang—some pure, white, loyal, and diligent, some with outstanding talent and excellence—are all good pillars of the altars of state; I hope Your Majesty will give them earnest attention, consult them on timely affairs, and have each exhaust his loyalty, picking up what has been omitted in one case out of ten thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xin, Lou Xuan, He Shao, Zhang Ti, Guo Chuo, Xue Ying, Teng Xiu, and my cousins Xi and Kang—men of integrity or exceptional talent—are pillars of the realm. Employ them, consult them on urgent matters, and let each give his utmost—lest one lapse in ten thousand undo us."

sentences.zh: 邵，齊之孫；

translations.literal: Shao was the grandson of He Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao was the grandson of He Qi.

sentences.zh: 瑩，綜之子；

translations.literal: Ying was the son of Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying was the son of Xue Zong.

sentences.zh: 玄，沛人；

translations.literal: Xuan was a man of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan came from Pei.

sentences.zh: 修，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Xiu was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu was a man of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 凱尋卒。

translations.literal: Kai soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Kai died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 呉主素銜其切直，且日聞何定之譖，久之，竟徙凱家於建安。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu had long resented his blunt directness, and daily heard He Ding's slanders; after a long time he finally relocated Kai's family to Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler had long resented Kai's bluntness; fed daily by He Ding's slanders, he eventually banished Kai's family to Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 呉主遣監軍虞汜、威南將軍薛珝、蒼梧太守丹楊陶璜從荊州道，監軍李勗、督軍徐存從建安海道，皆會於合浦，以撃交趾。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu sent Supervisory Commander Yu Si, Wei-nan General Xue Xu, and Cangwu Governor Tao Huang by the Jing Province route, and Supervisory Commander Li Xu and Overseer Xu Cun by the Jian'an sea route; all were to assemble at Hepu to strike Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler sent Yu Si, Xue Xu, and Tao Huang overland from Jing Province and Li Xu and Xu Cun by sea from Jian'an; all were to rendezvous at Hepu and attack Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，有司奏東宮施敬二傅，其儀不同。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the responsible officials memorialized that the Eastern Palace's observance toward the two tutors differed in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, officials noted that the crown prince's ritual toward his two tutors did not match precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「夫崇敬師傅，所以尊道重教也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "To respect and honor one's teachers is to honor the Way and value instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Honoring one's teachers honors the Way and upholds learning.

sentences.zh: 何言臣不臣乎！

translations.literal: How can one say that a subject is not a subject!
translations.idiomatic: How does that make the prince less a subject?

sentences.zh: 其令太子申拜禮。」

translations.literal: Order the crown prince to perform the bowing ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Let the crown prince perform the full bowing rite."

sentences.zh: 春，正月，呉丁奉入渦口，揚州刺史牽弘撃走之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Wu's Ding Feng entered Wokou; Yang Province Inspector Qian Hong struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Wu's Ding Feng raided Wokou; Yangzhou inspector Qian Hong repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 呉萬彧自巴丘還建業。

translations.literal: Wan Yu of Wu returned from Baling to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Yu withdrew from Baling to the Wu capital Jianye.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，呉左大司馬施績卒。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Wu's Left Grand Marshal Shi Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Wu left grand marshal Shi Ji died.

sentences.zh: 以鎭軍大將軍陸抗都督信陵、西陵、夷道、樂鄕、公安諸軍事，治樂鄕。

translations.literal: Military Defense Grand General Lu Kang was made to supervise military affairs at Xinling, Xiling, Yidao, Leyang, and Gong'an and administer from Leyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang, Military Defense grand general, took command at Xinling, Xiling, Yidao, Leyang, and Gong'an, with headquarters at Leyang.

sentences.zh: 抗以呉主政事多闕，上疎曰：「臣聞德均則衆者勝寡，力侔則安者制危，此六國所以並於秦、西楚所以屈於漢也。

translations.literal: Because the Lord of Wu's governance had many faults, Kang submitted a memorial, saying, "I hear that when virtue is equal the many overcome the few, and when strength is matched the secure control the perilous—this is why the six states were swallowed by Qin and Western Chu was bent by Han.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing many flaws in Wu's governance, Lu Kang memorialized: "When virtue is equal, numbers prevail; when strength is matched, the secure master the desperate—that is how Qin swallowed the six states and Han broke Western Chu.

sentences.zh: 今敵之所據，非特關右之地、鴻溝以西，而國家外無連衡之授，内非西楚之強，庶政陵遲，黎民未乂。

translations.literal: Now what the enemy holds is not only the lands west of the passes and Hong Canal; our state has no allied aid from without and inwardly lacks Western Chu's strength; various policies decline and the common people are not settled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy holds more than the western heartland; we have no allies abroad and lack Chu's old might at home; government falters and the people are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 議者所恃，徒以長江、峻山限帶封域；

translations.literal: What debaters rely on is only that the Yangtze and steep mountains bound and belt the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Counselors comfort themselves with the Yangtze and mountain barriers;

sentences.zh: 此乃守國之末事，非智者之所先也。

translations.literal: this is the last matter in defending a state, not what the wise put first.
translations.idiomatic: but that is the last line of defense, not what the wise plan first.

sentences.zh: 臣毎念及此，中夜撫枕，臨餐忘食。

translations.literal: Whenever I think of this I stroke the pillow in the middle of the night and forget food before my meal.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking on this, I clutch my pillow at midnight and lose my appetite at meals.

sentences.zh: 夫事君之義，犯而勿欺，謹陳時宜十七條以聞。」

translations.literal: The righteousness of serving one's lord is to admonish though it offend and not to deceive; I respectfully submit seventeen items on timely affairs for Your Majesty's hearing."
translations.idiomatic: To serve one's ruler is to speak plainly even when it stings; I respectfully offer seventeen recommendations on urgent affairs."

sentences.zh: 呉主不納。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler ignored the memorial.

sentences.zh: 李勗以建安道不利，殺導將馮斐，引軍還。

translations.literal: Li Xu, finding the Jian'an route unfavorable, killed the guide general Feng Fei and led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xu, judging the Jian'an route impracticable, executed guide general Feng Fei and withdrew his force.

sentences.zh: 初，何定嘗爲子求婚於勗，勗不許，乃白勗枉殺馮斐，擅徹軍還，誅勗及徐存，並其家屬，仍焚勗屍。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Ding had once sought a marriage for his son with Xu; Xu did not agree. Ding then reported that Xu had wrongly killed Feng Fei and had withdrawn the army on his own authority, and executed Xu and Xu Cun together with their dependents, then burned Xu's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: He Ding had once asked Li Xu for a son's marriage alliance; Xu refused. Ding then denounced Xu for killing Feng Fei without cause and withdrawing the army on his own authority, executed Xu and Xu Cun along with their families, and burned Xu's body.

sentences.zh: 定又使諸將各上御犬，一犬至直縑數十匹，纓紲直錢一萬，以捕兔供廚。

translations.literal: Ding also had each general present hunting dogs; one dog was worth several dozen bolts of plain silk, and collar and leash worth ten thousand cash, to catch rabbits for the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Ding ordered every general to furnish imperial hunting hounds—each animal valued at dozens of bolts of silk, its collar and leash at ten thousand cash—to supply the palace kitchens with rabbits.

sentences.zh: 呉人皆歸罪於定，而呉主以爲忠勤，賜爵列侯。

translations.literal: The people of Wu all laid the blame on Ding, but the Lord of Wu regarded him as loyal and diligent and bestowed the rank of Marquis among the Columns.
translations.idiomatic: Wu blamed He Ding for it all, yet Sun Hao called him loyal and diligent and made him a ranked marquis.

sentences.zh: 陸抗上疎曰：「小人不明理道，所見旣淺，雖使竭情盡節，猶不足任，況其奸心素篤而憎愛移易哉！」

translations.literal: Lu Kang submitted a memorial, saying, "Petty men do not understand principle and the Way; their vision is already shallow; even if they exhaust emotion and exhaust integrity, they are still not fit to be entrusted with office—how much less when their treacherous hearts are firmly set and love and hate shift easily!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang memorialized: "Men of low character grasp neither principle nor the Way; their vision is narrow. Even at full zeal they are unfit for trust—how much more when treachery runs deep and their favor turns on a whim!"

sentences.zh: 呉主不從。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊午，胡烈討鮮卑禿髮樹機能於萬斛堆，兵敗被殺。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day wuwu, Hu Lie campaigned against the Xianbei Tufa Shujineng at Wanhudui and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuwu, Hu Lie attacked the Xianbei leader Tufa Shujineng at Wanhudui, was routed, and killed.

sentences.zh: 都督雍、涼州諸軍事扶風王亮遣將軍劉旂救之，旂觀望不進。

translations.literal: Sima Liang of Fufeng, commander of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, sent General Liu Qi to rescue him; Qi watched and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Fufeng prince Sima Liang, commanding Yong and Liang, sent Liu Qi to the rescue; Qi hesitated on the march and never engaged.

sentences.zh: 亮坐貶爲平西將軍，旂當斬。

translations.literal: Liang was punished by demotion to Pacifier of the West General; Qi was to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was demoted to Pacifier of the West; Liu Qi was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 亮上言：「節度之咎，由亮而出，乞丐旂死。」

translations.literal: Liang submitted a statement: "The fault of command lies with Liang; I beg Qi be allowed to die."
translations.idiomatic: Liang pleaded: "Command failure rests on me—I ask that Liu Qi be spared execution."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「若罪不在旂，當有所在。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "If the guilt is not on Qi, there must be somewhere it lies."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "If Qi is not to blame, the guilt must lie elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 乃免亮官。

translations.literal: Liang's office was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書樂陵石鑒行安西將軍，都督秦州諸軍事，討樹機能。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing Shi Jian of Leling was sent as acting Pacifier of the West General to supervise military affairs in Qin Province and campaign against Shujineng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian of Leling was dispatched as acting Pacifier of the West to command Qin Province and suppress Shujineng.

sentences.zh: 樹機能兵盛，鑒使秦州刺史杜預出兵撃之。

translations.literal: Shujineng's troops were strong; Jian sent Qin Province Inspector Du Yu to lead troops out and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Shujineng's forces were formidable; Jian ordered Qin inspector Du Yu to take the field against him.

sentences.zh: 預以虜乘勝馬肥，而官軍縣乏，宜並力大運芻糧，須春進討。

translations.literal: Yu said that the barbarians, riding victory with fat horses, while the government army was short of supplies, should combine strength to transport fodder and grain in bulk and wait until spring to advance and campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu argued that the enemy, flush with victory and well-mounted, would overwhelm troops short on supplies; they should mass transport of fodder and grain and strike in spring.

sentences.zh: 鑒奏預稽乏軍興，檻車征詣廷尉，以贖論。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized that Yu was dilatory and deficient in raising the army, had him sent in a caged cart to the Minister of Justice, and he was sentenced by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Jian reported Du Yu for delaying the campaign; Yu was carted to the Minister of Justice and ransomed his sentence.

sentences.zh: 旣而鑒討樹機能，卒不能克。

translations.literal: Thereafter Jian campaigned against Shujineng but in the end could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then campaigned against Shujineng but failed to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙巳，城陽王景度卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day yisi, Prince Jingdu of Chengyang died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on yisi in the seventh month, Prince Jingdu of Chengyang died.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以汝陰王駿爲鎭西大將軍，都督雍、涼等州諸軍事，鎭關中。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the Prince of Ru'nan, Jun, was made Grand General Who Pacifies the West, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, and other provinces, and stationed to guard the passes.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Prince Ru'nan Sima Jun was named Grand General Who Pacifies the West, given Yong and Liang, and posted to guard Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，立皇子東爲汝南王。

translations.literal: In winter, in the eleventh month, the prince Dong was established as Prince of Ru'nan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, Prince Dong was enfeoffed as Prince of Ru'nan.

sentences.zh: 呉主從弟前將軍秀爲夏口督，呉主惡之，民間皆言秀當見圖。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu's younger cousin, former general Sun Xiu, was supervisor at Xiakou; the Lord of Wu hated him, and among the people all said Xiu would soon be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler's cousin, former general Sun Xiu, held Xiakou; Sun Hao distrusted him, and rumor held that Xiu would be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 會呉主遣何定將兵五千人獵夏口，秀驚，夜將妻子、親兵數百人來奔。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Wu sent He Ding to lead five thousand troops to hunt at Xiakou, Xiu was alarmed; at night he led his wife, several hundred personal troops, and kin to flee and submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt near Xiakou, Xiu panicked and fled by night with his wife, kin, and a few hundred guards to surrender to Jin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，拜秀驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，封會稽公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiu was appointed Rapid Cavalry General with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xiu was made Rapid Cavalry General with Three Excellencies privileges and Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 是歳，呉大赦。

translations.literal: That year, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wu declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初，魏人居南匈奴五部於并州諸郡，與中國民雜居；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wei had settled the five divisions of the Southern Xiongnu in the commanderies of Bing Province, mixed among the people of the Central States;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Wei had settled the five Southern Xiongnu divisions in Bing Province commanderies, intermingled with Han subjects;

sentences.zh: 自謂其先漢氏外孫，因改姓劉氏。

translations.literal: they considered themselves by descent grandsons of the Han house and therefore changed their surname to Liu.
translations.idiomatic: claiming descent from the Han imperial line, they took the surname Liu.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，匈奴右賢王劉猛叛出塞。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, the Xiongnu Right Worthy King Liu Meng rebelled and went beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Xiongnu Right Worthy King Liu Meng rebelled and fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史石鑒坐撃呉軍虚張首級，詔曰：「鑒備大臣，吾所取信，而乃下同爲詐，義得爾乎！

translations.literal: Yu Province Inspector Shi Jian was punished for attacking Wu troops and falsely inflating heads taken; the edict said, "Jian is a great minister whom I trust—yet he stooped to the same fraud as his subordinates; can righteousness be like this!
translations.idiomatic: Yu inspector Shi Jian was punished for inflating enemy heads after fighting Wu; the edict said: "Jian is a minister I trusted—yet he joined his men in fraud. Where is the righteousness in that?

sentences.zh: 今遣歸田里，終身不得復用。」

translations.literal: Now send him back to his village; he shall never again be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Send him home to his village and never employ him again."

sentences.zh: 呉人刁玄詐增讖文云：「黃旗紫蓋，見於東南，終有天下者，荊、揚之君。」

translations.literal: The Wu man Diao Xuan falsely augmented a prophecy text, saying, "Yellow banners and purple canopy appear in the southeast; in the end he who possesses All Under Heaven will be the lord of Jing and Yang."
translations.idiomatic: A Wu man named Diao Xuan forged a prophecy: "Yellow banners and a purple canopy will appear in the southeast—the ruler of Jing and Yang will win the realm."

sentences.zh: 呉主信之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao believed it.

sentences.zh: 是月晦，大舉兵出華里，載太后、皇后及後宮數千人，從牛渚西上。

translations.literal: On the last day of that month he raised a great army out of Huali, carrying the empress dowager, empress, and several thousand women of the rear palace, and went upriver from Niuzhu westward.
translations.idiomatic: On the month's last day he marched a huge host from Huali, taking the empress dowager, empress, and thousands of palace women upriver from Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 東觀令華譖等固諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Director of the Eastern Observatory Hua Yi and others firmly remonstrated; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Observatory director Hua Yi and others protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 行遇大雪，道塗陷壞，兵士被甲持仗，百人共引一車，寒凍殆死，皆曰：「若遇敵，便當倒戈。」

translations.literal: On the march they met heavy snow; roads and embankments collapsed; soldiers in armor bearing weapons—a hundred men together pulling one cart—were frozen nearly to death, and all said, "If we meet the enemy, we will at once turn our blades around."
translations.idiomatic: Snow blocked the roads; armored men had to haul wagons a hundred to a team and nearly froze. They muttered: "If we meet the enemy, we'll turn our blades around."

sentences.zh: 呉主聞之，乃還。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Wu heard of it, he turned back.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao heard, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 帝遣義陽王望統中軍二萬、騎三千屯壽春以備之，聞呉師退，乃罷。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Prince of Yiyang, Wang, to command twenty thousand central-army infantry and three thousand cavalry stationed at Shouchun to guard against them; when he heard the Wu army had withdrawn, he dismissed the force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Prince Yiyang Sima Wang with twenty thousand foot and three thousand horse to Shouchun; hearing Wu had withdrawn, he stood the army down.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌，巨鹿元公裴秀卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingxu, Duke Yuan of Julu, Pei Xiu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingxu, Pei Xiu, Duke Yuan of Julu, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，呉交州刺史陶璜襲九眞太守董元，殺之；

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Wu's Jiaozhi Inspector Tao Huang raided Jiuzhen Governor Dong Yuan and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Wu's Jiaozhi inspector Tao Huang raided Jiuzhen governor Dong Yuan and killed him;

sentences.zh: 楊稷以其將王素代之。

translations.literal: Yang Ji had his general Wang Su replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji installed his officer Wang Su as governor.

sentences.zh: 北地胡寇金城，涼州刺史牽弘討之。

translations.literal: The Hu of Beidi raided Jincheng; Liang Province Inspector Qian Hong campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: Beidi Hu raided Jincheng; Liang inspector Qian Hong marched against them.

sentences.zh: 衆胡皆内叛，與樹機能共圍弘於靑山，弘軍敗而死。

translations.literal: All the Hu rebelled inward and together with Shujineng besieged Hong at Qingshan; Hong's army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rose within and, with Shujineng, trapped Hong at Qingshan; his army was crushed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，大司馬陳騫言於帝曰：「胡烈、牽弘皆勇而無謀，強於自用，非綏邊之材也，將爲國恥。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Marshal Chen Qian had said to the emperor, "Hu Lie and Qian Hong are both brave but without strategy, strong in acting on their own judgment, not material for pacifying the frontier—they will become the state's shame."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Grand Marshal Chen Qian had warned the emperor: "Hu Lie and Qian Hong are brave but rash and self-willed—not men to pacify the frontier. They will bring the state shame."

sentences.zh: 時弘爲揚州刺史，多不承順騫命，帝以爲騫與弘不協而毀之，於是征弘，旣至，尋復以爲涼州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Hong was Yang Province Inspector and often did not follow Qian's orders; the emperor thought Qian was at odds with Hong and was slandering him, and therefore summoned Hong; once he arrived, he was soon again made Liang Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was then Yang inspector and often ignored Qian's orders; the emperor assumed personal rivalry and recalled Hong—only to send him back west as Liang inspector.

sentences.zh: 騫竊歎息，以爲必敗。

translations.literal: Qian sighed in private, thinking they would certainly fail.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sighed privately, certain they would fail.

sentences.zh: 二人果失羌戎之和，兵敗身沒，征討連年，僅而能定，帝乃悔之。

translations.literal: The two men indeed lost the harmony of the Qiang and Rong; their armies were defeated and they perished; campaigns followed year after year and only with difficulty was it settled; the emperor then regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Both lost the tribes' goodwill, were defeated and killed; campaigns dragged on for years before order returned—and the emperor regretted his choice.

sentences.zh: 五月，立皇子憲爲城陽王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Prince Xian was established as Prince of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Prince Xian was enfeoffed as Prince of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，義陽成王望卒。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the Accomplished Prince of Yiyang, Wang, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Prince Yiyang Sima Wang died.

sentences.zh: 侍中、尚書令、車騎將軍賈充，自文帝時寵任用事。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Cavalry General Jia Chong had from Emperor Wen's time been favored and employed in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Cavalry General Jia Chong had enjoyed favor and power since Emperor Wen's reign.

sentences.zh: 帝之爲太子，充頗有力，故益有寵於帝。

translations.literal: When the emperor was crown prince, Chong had been quite helpful, and therefore he had still more favor with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He had aided the emperor as crown prince, and his influence only grew after the succession.

sentences.zh: 充爲人巧諂，與太尉、行太子太傅荀顗、侍中、中書監荀勗、越騎校尉安平馮紞相爲黨友，朝野惡之。

translations.literal: Chong was crafty and fawning by nature; he, Grand Commandant and acting Crown Prince Grand Tutor Xun Yi, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretary Xun Xu, and Rapid Cavalry Commandant Feng Dan of Anping formed a clique of friends, and court and countryside detested them.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty and obsequious, Chong banded with Grand Commandant Xun Yi, Palace Secretary Xun Xu, and Rapid Cavalry Commandant Feng Dan; court and country loathed the clique.

sentences.zh: 帝問侍中裴楷以方今得失，對曰：「陛下受命，四海承風，所以未比德於堯、舜者，但以賈充之徒尚在朝耳。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Kai about the gains and losses of the present age; he replied, "Your Majesty received the Mandate and the four seas take the wind; the reason you have not yet matched the virtue of Yao and Shun is only that men like Jia Chong are still at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Attendant Pei Kai about the state's strengths and faults; Kai answered: "Your Majesty holds the Mandate and the realm obeys—yet you fall short of Yao and Shun chiefly because Jia Chong and his like still sit in court.

sentences.zh: 宜引天下賢人，與弘政道，不宜示人以私。

translations.literal: You ought to bring in the worthy of All Under Heaven and together broaden the way of government; you should not show people private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Summon the worthy from across the realm and govern openly—do not parade private favor.

sentences.zh: 侍中樂安任愷、河南尹穎川庾純皆與充不協，充欲解其近職，乃薦愷忠貞，宜在東宮；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Ren Kai of Le'an and Henan Intendant Yu Chun of Yingchuan were both at odds with Chong; Chong wished to remove them from close office and therefore recommended Kai as loyal and upright, fit for the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Ren Kai of Le'an and Henan intendant Yu Chun opposed Chong; Chong sought to move them from court and praised Kai's loyalty as fit for the heir's household—

sentences.zh: 帝以愷爲太子少傅，而侍中如故。

translations.literal: the emperor made Kai Crown Prince Junior Tutor while his attendant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor made Kai crown prince junior tutor but kept him as attendant.

sentences.zh: 會樹機能亂秦、雍，帝以爲憂，愷曰：「宜得威望重臣有智略者以鎭撫之。」

translations.literal: When Shujineng disturbed Qin and Yong, the emperor was troubled by it; Kai said, "You ought to obtain a great minister of prestige and weight with strategy and plan to pacify and settle it."
translations.idiomatic: When Shujineng ravaged Qin and Yong, the emperor was anxious; Kai said: "You need a senior commander of weight and strategy to pacify the frontier."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誰可者？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Who would do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Who would serve?"

sentences.zh: 愷因薦充，純亦稱之。

translations.literal: Kai thereupon recommended Chong, and Chun also praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai recommended Chong; Chun seconded him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉，以充爲都督秦、涼二州諸軍事，侍中、車騎將軍如故；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day guiyou, Chong was made commander of military affairs in Qin and Liang provinces; his posts as attendant and cavalry general remained as before;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on guiyou in the seventh month, Chong was named to command Qin and Liang while retaining attendant and cavalry general titles;

sentences.zh: 充患之。

translations.literal: Chong was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong dreaded the assignment.

sentences.zh: 呉大都督薛珝與陶璜等兵十萬，共攻交趾，城中糧盡援絶，爲呉所陷，虜楊稷、毛炅等。

translations.literal: Wu Grand Coordinator Xue Xu with Tao Huang and others, one hundred thousand troops together, attacked Jiaozhi; grain in the city was exhausted and relief cut off, and it fell to Wu; they captured Yang Ji, Mao Jing, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wu grand coordinator Xue Xu and Tao Huang led a hundred thousand men against Jiaozhi; when the city starved and relief failed, it fell; Yang Ji, Mao Jing, and others were taken.

sentences.zh: 璜愛炅勇健，欲活之，炅謀殺璜，璜乃殺之。

translations.literal: Huang admired Jing's courage and strength and wished to keep him alive; Jing plotted to kill Huang, and Huang therefore killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang admired Mao Jing's valor and meant to spare him; Jing plotted to kill Huang, and Huang executed him.

sentences.zh: 脩則之子允，生剖其腹，割其肝，曰：「復能作賊不？」

translations.literal: Xiu Ze's son Yun, while he was still alive, cut open his belly and sliced out his liver, saying, "Can you still be a bandit?
translations.idiomatic: Xiu Ze's son Yun, while Jing still lived, cut open his belly and carved out his liver, sneering: "Still playing rebel?

sentences.zh: 炅猶罵曰：「恨不殺汝孫皓，汝父何死狗也！」

translations.literal: Jing still cursed, saying, "I regret not having killed your grandson Hao—what kind of dead dog is your father!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing cursed to the end: "I only regret not killing your grandson Sun Hao—your father died like a cur!"

sentences.zh: 王素欲逃歸南中，呉人獲之，九眞、日南皆降於呉。

translations.literal: Wang Su wished to flee back to the southern interior; the Wu men captured him, and Jiuzhen and Rinan both submitted to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su tried to flee south; Wu seized him, and Jiuzhen and Rinan submitted.

sentences.zh: 呉大赦，以陶璜爲交州牧。

translations.literal: Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and made Tao Huang Inspector of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu amnestied the realm and made Tao Huang Jiaozhi inspector.

sentences.zh: 璜討降夷獠，州境皆平。

translations.literal: Huang campaigned against and received the submission of the Yi and Liao; the province's territory was all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huang subdued the tribal Yi and Liao until the province was quiet.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙申，城陽王憲卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bingshen, Prince Xian of Chengyang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingshen, Prince Xian of Chengyang died.

sentences.zh: 分益州南中四郡置寧州。

translations.literal: The four southern commanderies of the southern interior in Yi Province were separated to establish Ning Province.
translations.idiomatic: Four southern Yi Province commanderies were split off as Ning Province.

sentences.zh: 九月，呉司空孟仁卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wu's Minister of Works Meng Ren died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wu Minister of Works Meng Ren died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day dingchou of the tenth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，劉猛寇并州，并州刺史劉欽等撃破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Liu Meng raided Bing Province; Bing Province Inspector Liu Qin and others struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Liu Meng raided Bing; inspector Liu Qin routed him.

sentences.zh: 賈充將之鎭，公卿餞於夕陽亭。

translations.literal: Jia Chong was about to go to his command post; the dukes and ministers saw him off at Xiyang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: As Jia Chong prepared to take up frontier command, ministers saw him off at Xiyang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 充私問計於荀勗，勗曰：「公爲宰相，乃爲一夫所制，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Chong privately asked Xun Xu for a plan; Xu said, "You are chief minister yet are controlled by a single man—is that not base!
translations.idiomatic: Chong quietly asked Xun Xu for advice; Xu said: "You are chief minister yet one man dictates your fate—is that not shameful?

sentences.zh: 然是行也，辭之實難，獨有結婚太子，可不辭而自留矣。」

translations.literal: Yet this expedition is in truth hard to decline; only by marrying into the crown prince's house can you decline without declining and remain.
translations.idiomatic: Still, this posting is hard to refuse—only a marriage alliance with the heir can keep you at court without refusing outright."

sentences.zh: 充曰：「然孰可寄懷？」

translations.literal: Chong said, "So—but to whom can I entrust my hopes?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong asked: "Whom should I trust?"

sentences.zh: 勗曰：「勗請言之。」

translations.literal: Xu said, "Xu will speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "Leave it to me."

sentences.zh: 因謂馮紞曰：「賈公遠出，吾等失勢。

translations.literal: He then said to Feng Dan, "When Master Jia goes far away, we lose our power.
translations.idiomatic: He told Feng Dan: "Once Jia leaves, we lose our footing.

sentences.zh: 太子婚尚未定，何不勸帝納賈公之女乎！」

translations.literal: The crown prince's marriage is not yet settled—why not urge the emperor to take Master Jia's daughter!"
translations.idiomatic: The heir's marriage is unsettled—urge the emperor to take Jia's daughter!"

sentences.zh: 紞亦然之。

translations.literal: Dan also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，帝將納衞瓘女爲太子妃，充妻郭槐賂楊后左右，使后説帝，求納其女。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor was about to take Wei Guan's daughter as crown princess; Chong's wife Guo Huai bribed the empress's attendants to have the empress speak to the emperor and seek to have her own daughter taken in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had favored Wei Guan's daughter for crown princess; Chong's wife Guo Huai bribed the empress's women to plead for her daughter.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「衞公女有五可，賈公女有五不可：衞氏種賢而多子，美而長、白；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The Wei clan's daughter has five positives; Master Jia's daughter has five negatives: the Wei stock is worthy and has many sons, beautiful, tall, and fair;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wei's daughter has five virtues; Jia's has five faults—Wei's line is noble and fertile, her beauty tall and fair;

sentences.zh: 賈氏種妬而少子，丑而短、黑。」

translations.literal: the Jia stock is jealous and has few sons, ugly, short, and dark."
translations.idiomatic: Jia's line is jealous and barren, her looks short and dark."

sentences.zh: 后固以爲請，荀顗、荀勗、馮瓘皆稱充女絶美，且有才德，帝遂從之。

translations.literal: The empress firmly pressed the request; Xun Yi, Xun Xu, and Feng Dan all praised Chong's daughter as surpassingly beautiful and moreover possessing talent and virtue, and the emperor followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress pressed hard; Xun Yi, Xun Xu, and Feng Dan praised Jia's daughter as peerless in beauty and talent—and the emperor yielded.

sentences.zh: 留充復居舊任。

translations.literal: Chong was kept and again held his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was kept at his old posts.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以光祿大夫鄭袤爲司空，袤固辭不受。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Palace Counselor Zheng Mao was made Minister of Works; Mao firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Palace Counselor Zheng Mao was offered Minister of Works; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 是歳，安樂思公劉禪卒。

translations.literal: That year, the Reflective Duke of Anle, Liu Shan, died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Shan, Reflective Duke of Anle, died.

sentences.zh: 呉以武昌都督廣陵范愼爲太尉。

translations.literal: Wu made Wuchang Supervisor Fan Shen of Guangling Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wu made Wuchang supervisor Fan Shen of Guangling grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 右將軍司馬丁奉卒。

translations.literal: Right General Sima Dingfeng died.
translations.idiomatic: Right general Ding Feng died.

sentences.zh: 呉改明年元曰鳳凰。

translations.literal: Wu changed the next year's era name to Fenghuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu adopted the reign title Fenghuang for the coming year.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，監軍何楨討劉猛，屢破之，潛以利誘其左部帥李恪，恪殺猛以降。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, supervisory commander He Zhen campaigned against Liu Meng, repeatedly defeating him; he secretly used profit to entice Meng's left division commander Li Ke; Ke killed Meng and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, supervisory commander He Zhen repeatedly defeated Liu Meng, then bribed his left commander Li Ke, who killed Meng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，皇太子納賈妃。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinmao, the crown prince took Consort Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, the crown prince wed Lady Jia.

sentences.zh: 妃年十五，長於太子二歳，妬忌多權詐，太子嬖而畏之。

translations.literal: The consort was fifteen, two years older than the crown prince, jealous and full of crafty power; the crown prince doted on her yet feared her.
translations.idiomatic: She was fifteen—two years older than the heir—jealous and scheming; he adored and feared her.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，安平獻王孚卒，年九十三。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, the Accomplished Prince of Anping, Fu, died, aged ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Prince Anping Sima Fu died at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 孚性忠愼，宣帝執政，孚常自退損。

translations.literal: Fu's nature was loyal and cautious; when the Emperor Xuan wielded government, Fu often withdrew and diminished himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was loyal and cautious; under Emperor Xuan he always kept a modest distance from power.

sentences.zh: 後逢廢立之際，未嘗預謀。

translations.literal: Later, at the time of deposition and establishment, he never took part in plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Through the coups that raised and deposed emperors, he never plotted.

sentences.zh: 景、文二帝以孚屬尊，亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: Emperors Jing and Wen, because Fu's rank was exalted, also did not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Jing and Wen, respecting his seniority, never pressed him.

sentences.zh: 及帝卽位，恩禮尤重。

translations.literal: When the present emperor succeeded, favor and ritual were especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present emperor his honors were especially lavish.

sentences.zh: 元會，詔孚乘輿上殿，帝於阼階迎拜。

translations.literal: At the yuan assembly, an edict ordered Fu to ride the imperial carriage up the hall; the emperor at the throne steps came down to meet and bow.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year audience the emperor had Fu ride the imperial carriage to the hall and met him bowing at the throne steps.

sentences.zh: 旣坐，親奉觴上壽，如家人禮。

translations.literal: Once seated, he personally offered the cup for longevity with the ritual of a family.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, he personally offered the longevity cup with family ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝毎拜，孚跪而止之。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor bowed, Fu knelt to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the emperor bowed, Fu knelt to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 孚雖見尊寵，不以爲榮，常有憂色。

translations.literal: Though Fu was shown honor and favor, he did not regard it as glory and often wore a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: Though honored at court, Fu took no pride in it and often looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 臨終，遺令曰：「有魏貞士河内司馬孚字叔達，不伊不周，不夷不惠，立身行道，終始若一。

translations.literal: At his end he left instructions, saying, "There was a loyal gentleman of Wei, Sima Fu of Henei, styled Shuda—not Yi, not Zhou, not Boyi, not Bian He; in establishing himself and walking the Way, from beginning to end he was one.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he wrote: "I am Sima Fu of Henei, styled Shuda, a loyal gentleman of Wei—neither partisan nor recluse, neither zealot nor cynic; in conduct I have been one man from first to last.

sentences.zh: 當衣以時服，斂以素棺。」

translations.literal: He should be clothed in seasonal dress and encoffined in a plain coffin."
translations.idiomatic: Dress me in ordinary clothes and bury me in a plain coffin."

sentences.zh: 詔賜東園温明秘器，諸所施行，皆依漢東平獻王故事。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the Eastern Garden warm-bright secret vessels; all procedures followed the precedent of the Han Prince Xian of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the Eastern Garden funeral regalia and followed Han precedent for Prince Xian of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 其家遵孚遺旨，所給器物，一不施用。

translations.literal: His family followed Fu's last wishes; of the objects given, not one was used.
translations.idiomatic: The family obeyed his will and used none of the imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 帝與右將國皇甫陶論事，陶與帝爭言，散騎常侍鄭徽表請罪之，帝曰：「忠讜之言，唯患不聞。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed affairs with Right General of the State Huangfu Tao; Tao disputed with the emperor in speech. Regular Attendant Zheng Hui memorialized asking that Tao be punished; the emperor said, "Loyal and forthright words—I only fear not hearing them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor debated policy with Right General Huangfu Tao, who spoke bluntly. Regular Attendant Zheng Hui asked that Tao be punished; the emperor said: "I only fear not hearing honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 徽越職妄奏，豈朕之意！」

translations.literal: Hui overstepped his office and rashly memorialized—how is that my intent!
translations.idiomatic: Hui overstepped his office—how is that my intent!"

sentences.zh: 遂免徽官。

translations.literal: Hui's office was then removed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was dismissed instead.

sentences.zh: 夏，汶山白馬胡侵掠諸種，益州刺史皇甫晏欲討之。

translations.literal: In summer, the White Horse Hu of Wenshan raided the various tribes; Yi Province Inspector Huangfu Yan wished to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the Wenshan White Horse Hu raided tribal lands; Yi inspector Huangfu Yan prepared to attack.

sentences.zh: 典學從事蜀郡何旅等諫曰：「胡夷相殘，固其常性，未爲大患。

translations.literal: Classics Instructor He Lü of Shu Commandery and others remonstrated, saying, "Hu and Yi slaughter one another by nature—it is not yet a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Classics instructor He Lü of Shu and others warned: "Barbarians fighting one another is their custom—not yet a grave threat.

sentences.zh: 今盛夏出軍，水潦將降，必有疾疫，宜須秋、冬圖之。」

translations.literal: Now to send out the army in midsummer, when floods are about to fall, there will certainly be pestilence; you ought to wait for autumn and winter and then plan it."
translations.idiomatic: A summer campaign means floods and plague—wait until autumn or winter."

sentences.zh: 晏不聽。

translations.literal: Yan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 胡康木子燒香言軍出必敗，晏以爲沮衆，斬之。

translations.literal: The Hu Kang Muzi burned incense and said that if the army went out it would certainly be defeated; Yan thought he was discouraging the troops and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: A Hu shaman named Kang Muzi burned incense and prophesied defeat; Yan executed him for demoralizing the army.

sentences.zh: 軍至觀阪，牙門張弘等以汶山道險，且畏胡衆，因夜作亂，殺晏，軍中驚擾，兵曹從事犍爲楊倉勒兵力戰而死。

translations.literal: When the army reached Guanban, Gate Officer Zhang Hong and others, because the Wenshan road was perilous and they also feared the Hu masses, made a night mutiny, killed Yan, and threw the army into alarm; Military Affairs Clerk Yang Cang of Jianwei led troops in fierce fighting and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Guanban, gate officer Zhang Hong and others, fearing the narrow Wenshan road and the Hu, mutinied by night, killed Yan, and threw the army into chaos; military clerk Yang Cang of Jianwei fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 弘遂誣晏，云「率己共反」，故殺之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Hong then slandered Yan, saying, "He led us together in rebellion," and therefore killed him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then claimed Yan had led a mutiny, killed him, and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晏主簿蜀郡何攀，方居母喪，聞之，詣洛證晏不反，弘等縱兵抄掠。

translations.literal: Yan's chief clerk He Pan of Shu Commandery was in mourning for his mother; when he heard of it, he went to Luoyang to prove Yan had not rebelled, while Hong and others let their troops plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's chief clerk He Pan of Shu, though mourning his mother, hurried to Luoyang to prove Yan's innocence while Hong's men looted.

sentences.zh: 廣漢主簿李毅言於太守弘農王濬曰：「皇甫侯起自諸生，何求而反！

translations.literal: Guanghan chief clerk Li Yi said to the prefect, Prince Jun of Hongnong, "Inspector Huangfu rose from the scholar class—what would he seek by rebelling!
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan chief clerk Li Yi told prefect Prince Jun of Hongnong: "Huangfu Yan was a scholar-official—what could he gain by rebellion?

sentences.zh: 且廣漢與成都密邇，而統於梁州者，朝廷欲以制益州之衿領，正防今日之變也。

translations.literal: Moreover Guanghan is close to Chengdu yet subordinate to Liang Province because the court wished thereby to control Yi Province's throat—precisely to guard against today's change.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan lies near Chengdu yet answers to Liang Province precisely so the court can choke Yi's throat—this crisis is exactly what that arrangement was meant to prevent.

sentences.zh: 今益州有亂，乃此郡之憂也。

translations.literal: Now that Yi Province has disorder, it is this commandery's worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province's turmoil is our commandery's crisis.

sentences.zh: 張弘小豎，衆所不與，宜卽時赴討，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Hong is a petty fellow whom the masses do not support; you ought to go at once to campaign against him and not miss the chance."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong is a nobody the troops despise—strike now or lose the chance."

sentences.zh: 濬欲先上請，毅曰：「殺主之賊，爲惡尤大，當不拘常制，何請之有！」

translations.literal: Jun wished first to memorialize and request permission; Yi said, "A murderer of his lord commits the greatest evil; he should not be bound by regular regulations—what need to request!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun wanted to ask the court first; Yi said: "Killing one's commander is the gravest crime—no time for formalities!"

sentences.zh: 濬乃發兵討弘。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon raised troops to campaign against Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun marched against Hong.

sentences.zh: 詔以濬爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict made Jun Yi Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Jun Yi Province inspector.

sentences.zh: 濬撃弘，斬之，夷三族。

translations.literal: Jun struck Hong, beheaded him, and exterminated three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Jun killed Hong and exterminated his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 封濬關内侯。

translations.literal: Jun was enfeoffed as Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was enfeoffed as a marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 初，濬爲羊祜參軍，祜深知之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jun had been Yang Hu's aide; Hu knew him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had served as Yang Hu's aide; Hu knew his worth.

sentences.zh: 祜兄子暨白濬「爲人志大奢侈，不可專任，宜有以裁之。」

translations.literal: Hu's brother's son Ji told Jun, "As a man his ambition is great and he is extravagant; he cannot be solely entrusted—there ought to be means to restrain him."
translations.idiomatic: Hu's nephew Ji warned Jun: "He is ambitious and extravagant—do not give him sole authority without checks."

sentences.zh: 祜曰：「濬有大才，將以濟其所欲，必可用也。」

translations.literal: Hu said, "Jun has great talent; he will use it to achieve what he desires and can certainly be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Hu replied: "Jun has great talent; let him pursue his aims and he will serve us well."

sentences.zh: 更轉爲車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was transferred to the cavalry secretariat.

sentences.zh: 濬在益州，明立威信，蠻夷多歸附之；

translations.literal: Jun in Yi Province clearly established prestige and trust, and many of the barbarians submitted to him;
translations.idiomatic: In Yi Province Jun won trust and many tribes submitted;

sentences.zh: 俄遷大司農。

translations.literal: soon he was moved to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: soon he was promoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時帝與羊祜陰謀伐呉，祜以爲伐呉宜藉上流之勢，密表留濬復爲益州刺史，使治水軍。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor and Yang Hu secretly plotted to attack Wu; Hu thought that attacking Wu should borrow the advantage of the upper stream and secretly memorialized to retain Jun again as Yi Province Inspector and have him build a water army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Yang Hu were plotting against Wu; Hu argued the attack must use the upper Yangtze and secretly had Jun returned to Yi as inspector to build a river fleet.

sentences.zh: 尋加龍驤將軍，監益、梁諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Dragon Cavalry General and supervised military affairs in Yi and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named Dragon Cavalry General overseeing Yi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 詔濬罷屯田兵，大作舟艦。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jun to dismiss the garrison-farming troops and build ships on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Jun to disband garrison farmers and build a great fleet.

sentences.zh: 別駕何攀以爲「屯田兵不過五六百人，作船不能猝辦，後者未成，前者已腐。

translations.literal: Deputy Inspector He Pan thought, "The garrison-farming troops are no more than five or six hundred men; building ships cannot be done in a rush—the later ones are not finished before the earlier have rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy inspector He Pan argued: "Garrison farmers number only five or six hundred—ships built that slowly will rot before they launch.

sentences.zh: 宜召諸郡兵合萬餘人造之，歳終可成。」

translations.literal: You ought to summon troops from the commanderies together, more than ten thousand men to build them; by year's end they can be completed."
translations.idiomatic: Summon more than ten thousand men from the commanderies; the fleet can be ready within the year."

sentences.zh: 濬欲先上須報，攀曰：「朝廷猝聞召萬兵，必不聽；

translations.literal: Jun wished first to memorialize and await reply; Pan said, "If the court suddenly hears of summoning ten thousand troops, it will certainly not consent;
translations.idiomatic: Jun wanted court approval first; Pan said: "If the court hears you are raising ten thousand men, it will refuse—

sentences.zh: 不如輒召，設當見卻，功夫已成，勢不得止。」

translations.literal: better to summon them at once; even if you should be rebuked, once the work is done the momentum cannot be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: better summon them now; even if rebuked, once the work is done they cannot stop you."

sentences.zh: 濬從之，令攀典造舟艦器仗。

translations.literal: Jun followed his advice and ordered Pan to oversee building ships, weapons, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed and put Pan in charge of shipbuilding and armaments.

sentences.zh: 於是作大艦，長百二十歩，受二千餘人，以木爲城，起樓櫓，開四出門，其上皆得馳馬往來。

translations.literal: Thereupon they built great vessels a hundred and twenty paces long, holding more than two thousand men, with wood fashioned as ramparts, towers and watchtowers raised, four gates opening outward—on them one could ride horses back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: They built giants a hundred twenty paces long, each holding two thousand men, with wooden ramparts, towers, and four gates wide enough for horsemen to ride through.

sentences.zh: 時作船木柿，蔽江而下，呉建平太守呉郡吾彦取流柿以白呉主曰：「晉必有攻呉之計，宜增建平兵以塞其衝要。」

translations.literal: At that time the wood chips from shipbuilding covered the river flowing down; Wu's Jianping Inspector Wu Yan of Wu Commandery took the floating chips and reported to the Lord of Wu, saying, "Jin certainly has a plan to attack Wu; you ought to increase Jianping troops to block their vital points."
translations.idiomatic: Shipbuilding chips choked the river downstream; Wu's Jianping inspector Wu Yan collected the driftwood and warned Sun Hao: "Jin is preparing to attack—reinforce Jianping and block the Yangtze throat."

sentences.zh: 呉主不從。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 彦乃爲鐵鎖橫斷江路。

translations.literal: Yan therefore made iron chains stretched across to block the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Yan stretched iron chains across the river instead.

sentences.zh: 王濬雖受中制募兵，而無虎符；

translations.literal: Wang Jun though receiving the central command to raise troops, had no tiger tally;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun had imperial authorization to raise troops but no tiger tally;

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守敦煌張斆收濬從事列上。

translations.literal: Guanghan Inspector Zhang Xiao of Dunhuang arrested Jun's clerks and listed them in a report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan inspector Zhang Xiao of Dunhuang arrested Jun's staff and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 帝召斅還，責曰：「何不密啓而便收從事？」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xiao back and reproached him, saying, "Why did you not secretly report but at once arrest the clerks?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Xiao and rebuked him: "Why arrest his staff instead of reporting privately?"

sentences.zh: 斆曰：「蜀、漢絶遠，劉備嘗用之矣。

translations.literal: Xiao said, "Shu and Han are utterly remote; Liu Bei once used such measures.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao replied: "Shu is far from the capital—Liu Bei once did the same.

sentences.zh: 輒收，臣猶以爲輕。」

translations.literal: To arrest at once—I still thought it light."
translations.idiomatic: Even immediate arrest seemed too mild to me."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以賈充爲司空，侍中、尚書令、領兵如故。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Jia Chong was made Minister of Works; his posts as attendant, director of the Masters of Writing, and command of troops remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Jia Chong was made Minister of Works while retaining attendant, director, and troop commands.

sentences.zh: 充與侍中任愷皆爲帝所寵任，充欲專名勢，而忌愷，於是朝士各有所附，朋黨紛然。

translations.literal: Chong and Attendant-in-Ordinary Ren Kai were both favored and entrusted by the emperor; Chong wished to monopolize fame and power and resented Kai, and therefore court gentlemen each had their attachments and factions swarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and attendant Ren Kai were both favorites; Chong sought sole dominance and resented Kai, and court factions formed.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，召充、愷宴於式乾殿而謂之曰：「朝廷宜一，大臣當和。」

translations.literal: The emperor knew of it, summoned Chong and Kai to feast in the Shiqian Hall and said to them, "The court ought to be one; great ministers ought to be harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned both to feast in Shiqian Hall and said: "The court must be united; ministers must be at peace."

sentences.zh: 充、愷各拜謝。

translations.literal: Chong and Kai each bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Both bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 旣而充、愷以帝已知而不責，愈無所憚，外相崇重，内怨益深。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chong and Kai, because the emperor knew yet did not punish, were all the more without restraint; outwardly they mutually honored one another, while inwardly resentment grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor would not punish them, they grew bolder—outward courtesy, inward hatred.

sentences.zh: 充乃薦愷爲吏部尚書，愷侍覲轉希，充因與荀勗、馮紞承間共譖之，愷由是得罪，廢於家。

translations.literal: Chong then recommended Kai as Director of the Masters of Personnel; Kai's attendance at audience grew rare; Chong, together with Xun Xu and Feng Dan, seized opportunities to slander him together, and Kai thereby fell into guilt and was dismissed to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had Kai made personnel director, then with Xun Xu and Feng Dan slandered him until Kai was ruined and sent home.

sentences.zh: 八月，呉主征昭武將軍、西陵督歩闡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Lord of Wu summoned Rapid Tiger General and Xiling Supervisor Bu Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Wu ruler summoned Rapid Tiger general and Xiling supervisor Bu Chan.

sentences.zh: 闡世在西陵，猝被徽，自以失職，且懼有讒，九月，據城來降，遣兄子璣、璿詣洛陽爲任。

translations.literal: Chan's family had for generations been at Xiling; suddenly he received the summons and thought he had lost his post and also feared slander; in the ninth month he held the city and came to surrender, sending his brother's sons Ji and Xuan to Luoyang as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The Bu clan had held Xiling for generations; the sudden summons convinced Chan he was disgraced and doomed; in the ninth month he surrendered the city and sent his nephews Ji and Xuan to Luoyang as hostages.

sentences.zh: 詔以闡爲都督西陵諸軍事、衞將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中，領交州牧，封宜都公。

translations.literal: An edict made Chan commander of military affairs at Xiling, Defender General, credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, attendant-in-ordinary, and concurrently Inspector of Jiaozhi, enfeoffed as Duke of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Chan Xiling commander, Defender General with Three Excellencies honors, attendant, Jiaozhi inspector, and Duke of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day xinwei, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day xinwei of the tenth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守尹璩卒。

translations.literal: Dunhuang Inspector Yin Fan died.
translations.idiomatic: Dunhuang inspector Yin Fan died.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史楊欣表敦煌令梁澄領太守。

translations.literal: Liang Province Inspector Yang Xin memorialized that Dunhuang Magistrate Liang Cheng act as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Liang inspector Yang Xin recommended Dunhuang magistrate Liang Cheng as acting inspector.

sentences.zh: 功曹宋質輒廢澄，表議郎令狐豐爲太守。

translations.literal: Recorder Song Zhi at once deposed Cheng and memorialized that Gentleman for Discussion Linghu Feng be inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Song Zhi deposed Cheng and named Gentleman for Discussion Linghu Feng inspector.

sentences.zh: 楊欣遣兵之計，爲質所敗。

translations.literal: Yang Xin sent troops to punish him and was defeated by Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin sent troops against him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 呉陸抗聞歩闡叛，亟遣將軍左弈、吾彦等討之。

translations.literal: Wu's Lu Kang, hearing that Bu Chan had rebelled, urgently sent Generals Zuo Yi and Wu Yan and others to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Bu Chan's defection, Wu's Lu Kang sent Zuo Yi, Wu Yan, and others to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 帝遣荊州刺史楊肇迎闡於西陵，車騎將軍羊祜帥歩軍出江陵，巴東監軍徐胤帥水軍撃建平，以救闡。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Jing Province Inspector Yang Zhao to welcome Chan at Xiling; Cavalry General Yang Hu led infantry out of Jiangling; Badong supervisory commander Xu Yin led the water army to strike Jianping, to rescue Chan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Jing inspector Yang Zhao to relieve Xiling, cavalry general Yang Hu with infantry from Jiangling, and Badong supervisor Xu Yin with the fleet against Jianping—all to save Chan.

sentences.zh: 陸抗敕西陵諸軍築嚴圍，自赤谿至於故市，内以圍闡，外以御晉兵，晝夜催切，如敵已至，衆甚苦之。

translations.literal: Lu Kang ordered the Xiling armies to build a strict encirclement from Chixi to the old market, within to besiege Chan and without to resist Jin troops, urging day and night as if the enemy had already arrived; the masses suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang ringed Xiling from Chixi to the old market, besieging Chan within and blocking Jin without, driving the work day and night as if the enemy were already there—the troops suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 諸將諫曰：「今宜及三軍之鋭，急攻闡，比晉救至，必可拔也，何事於圍，以敝士民之力！」

translations.literal: The generals remonstrated, saying, "Now you ought to take advantage of the three armies' sharp edge and press the attack on Chan; before Jin relief arrives it can certainly be taken—why trouble with encirclement to exhaust the strength of officers and people!"
translations.idiomatic: Generals urged: "Strike now with the army's full edge—take Chan before Jin arrives! Why exhaust men building walls?"

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「此城處勢旣固，糧穀又足，且凡備御之具，皆抗所宿規，今反攻之，不可猝拔。

translations.literal: Kang said, "This city's position is already firm and grain is sufficient; moreover all defensive equipment was long planned by Kang; to attack it now cannot be taken in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: Kang replied: "The position is strong, grain ample, and every defense was of my own design—an assault cannot succeed quickly.

sentences.zh: 北兵至而無備，表裡受難，何以御之！」

translations.literal: When northern troops arrive and there is no preparation, inside and outside will suffer hardship—how can we resist them!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jin comes we will be caught inside and out—how then can we hold?"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆欲攻闡，抗欲服衆心，聽令一攻，果無利。

translations.literal: The generals all wished to attack Chan; Kang wished to satisfy the multitude's hearts and permitted one attack—it indeed brought no gain.
translations.idiomatic: The generals still wanted to attack; to convince them Kang allowed one assault—it failed as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 圍備始合，而羊祜兵五萬至江陵。

translations.literal: The encirclement was just completed when Yang Hu's fifty thousand troops reached Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The ring had just closed when Yang Hu's fifty thousand men reached Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸以抗不宜上，抗曰：「江陵城固兵足，無可憂者。

translations.literal: The generals all thought Kang ought not go upriver; Kang said, "Jiangling's walls are firm and troops ample—there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Officers said Kang should not march upstream; he answered: "Jiangling is strong and well garrisoned—

sentences.zh: 假令敵得江陵，必不能守，所損者小。

translations.literal: Even if the enemy took Jiangling, they certainly could not hold it; the loss would be small.
translations.idiomatic: even if the enemy took Jiangling they could not hold it—the loss would be slight.

sentences.zh: 若晉據西陵，則南山群夷皆當擾動，其患不可量也！」

translations.literal: If Jin holds Xiling, then the tribal peoples of the southern mountains will all be stirred to movement—the calamity cannot be measured!"
translations.idiomatic: But if Jin holds Xiling, the southern mountain tribes will rise—the disaster would be beyond measure!"

sentences.zh: 乃自帥衆赴西陵。

translations.literal: He thereupon himself led the multitude to go to Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to Xiling himself.

sentences.zh: 初，抗以江陵之北，道路平易，敕江陵督張咸作大堰遏水，漸漬平土以絶寇叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kang, because north of Jiangling the roads were level and easy, had ordered Jiangling Supervisor Zhang Xian to build a great dam to hold back water, gradually soaking the level land to cut off bandit rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kang had ordered Jiangling supervisor Zhang Xian to dam the easy roads north of Jiangling and flood the flats to block raiders.

sentences.zh: 羊祜欲因所遏水以船運糧，揚聲將破堰以通歩軍。

translations.literal: Yang Hu wished to use the held-back water to transport grain by boat and spread word that he would break the dam to open a route for infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu planned to ship grain through the reservoir and publicly threatened to breach the dam for an infantry route.

sentences.zh: 抗聞之，使咸亟破之。

translations.literal: Kang heard of it and ordered Xian to break it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Kang heard and ordered Xian to destroy the dam at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆惑，屢諫，不聽。

translations.literal: The generals were all perplexed and remonstrated repeatedly; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were baffled and protested repeatedly; he ignored them.

sentences.zh: 祜至當陽，聞堰敗，乃改船以車運糧，大費功力。

translations.literal: When Hu reached Dangyang and heard the dam was broken, he changed from boats to carts to transport grain, greatly wasting labor.
translations.idiomatic: Hu reached Dangyang, found the dam gone, and hauled grain by cart at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 十一月，楊肇至西陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yang Zhao reached Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yang Zhao reached Xiling.

sentences.zh: 陸抗令公安督孫遵循南岸御羊祜，水軍督留慮拒徐胤，抗自將大軍憑圍對肇。

translations.literal: Lu Kang ordered Gong'an Supervisor Sun Zun to follow the south bank and resist Yang Hu; Water Army Supervisor Liu Lü to resist Xu Yin; Kang himself led the great army leaning on the encirclement to face Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang posted Gong'an supervisor Sun Zun on the south bank against Yang Hu, water commander Liu Lü against Xu Yin, and faced Zhao with the main force behind the siege lines.

sentences.zh: 將軍朱喬營都督兪贊亡詣肇。

translations.literal: General Zhu Qiao's camp supervisor Yu Zan fled and went to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhu Qiao's camp supervisor Yu Zan defected to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「贊軍中舊吏，知吾虚實。

translations.literal: Kang said, "Zan is an old clerk in the army and knows our emptiness and fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Kang said: "Zan knows our dispositions—

sentences.zh: 吾常慮夷兵素不簡練，若敵攻圍，必先此處。」

translations.literal: I have always worried that the tribal troops are by nature not well trained; if the enemy attacks the encirclement, they will certainly strike this place first."
translations.idiomatic: I have always feared our tribal auxiliaries are poorly trained; if the enemy assaults the ring, they will strike here first."

sentences.zh: 卽夜易夷兵，皆以精兵守之。

translations.literal: That very night he exchanged the tribal troops and all used crack troops to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: That night he replaced the tribal guards with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 明日，肇果攻故夷兵處。

translations.literal: The next day, Zhao indeed attacked the former tribal troop position.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhao attacked exactly that sector.

sentences.zh: 抗命撃之，矢石雨下，肇衆傷、死者相屬。

translations.literal: Kang ordered the strike; arrows and stones fell like rain; Zhao's multitude wounded and dead followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Kang counterattacked; arrows and stones rained down; Zhao's men fell in heaps.

sentences.zh: 十二月，肇計屈，夜遁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhao's plans were exhausted and he fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhao's plans failed and he fled by night.

sentences.zh: 抗欲追之，而慮歩闡畜力伺間，兵不足分，於是但鳴鼓戒衆，若將追者。

translations.literal: Kang wished to pursue but feared Bu Chan would husband strength and watch for an opening, and troops were insufficient to divide; he therefore only beat drums to warn the multitude as if about to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Kang wanted to pursue but feared Chan would strike if he divided his force; he only beat drums as if giving chase.

sentences.zh: 肇衆兇懼，悉解甲挺走。

translations.literal: Zhao's multitude, fierce and afraid, all doffed armor and ran with spears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's terrified troops threw off armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 抗使輕兵躡之，肇兵大敗，祜等皆引軍還。

translations.literal: Kang sent light troops to follow them; Zhao's army suffered a great defeat; Hu and the others all led their armies back.
translations.idiomatic: Light troops harried them; Zhao was routed; Hu and the others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 抗遂拔西陵，誅闡及同謀將吏數十人，皆夷三族，自餘所請赦者數萬口。

translations.literal: Kang thereupon took Xiling, executed Chan and several tens of plotting officers and officials, all exterminating three clans; apart from these, those he requested to pardon numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Kang took Xiling, executed Chan and dozens of conspirators with their clans to the third degree, and spared tens of thousands besides.

sentences.zh: 東還樂鄕，貌無矜色，謙沖如常。

translations.literal: Returning east to Lexiang, his appearance showed no air of pride; he was modest and restrained as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Lexiang without a trace of triumph, as modest as ever.

sentences.zh: 呉主加抗都護。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu added to Kang the post of Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao made Kang grand coordinator as well.

sentences.zh: 羊祜坐貶平南將軍，楊肇免爲庶人。

translations.literal: Yang Hu was punished by demotion to Pacifier of the South General; Yang Zhao was removed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu was demoted to Pacifier of the South; Yang Zhao was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 呉主旣克西陵，自謂得天助，志益張大，使術士尚廣筮取天下，對曰：「吉。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu, having taken Xiling, thought himself aided by Heaven; his ambition grew still greater; he had the technician Shang Guang divine for All Under Heaven; he replied, "Auspicious.
