translations.idiomatic: After taking Xiling, Sun Hao thought Heaven favored him; his ambitions swelled; technician Shang Guang divined the realm's fate and answered: "Auspicious.

sentences.zh: 庚子歳，靑蓋當入洛陽。」

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, the blue canopy will enter Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi year the imperial canopy will enter Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 呉主喜，不修德政，專爲兼併之計。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu was pleased and did not cultivate virtuous government but specialized in plans of annexation.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Sun Hao neglected virtue and threw himself into schemes of conquest.

sentences.zh: 賈充與朝士宴飲，河南尹庾純醉，與充爭言。

translations.literal: Jia Chong feasted with court gentlemen; Henan Intendant Yu Chun, drunk, disputed with Chong in speech.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast with courtiers, drunken Henan intendant Yu Chun quarreled with Jia Chong.

sentences.zh: 充曰：「父老，不歸供養，卿爲無天地！」

translations.literal: Chong said, "You are old and do not return to support your parents—you are without Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: Chong sneered: "You're old yet neglect your parents—you have no regard for Heaven and Earth!

sentences.zh: 純曰：「髙貴鄕公何在？」

translations.literal: Chun said, "Where is the Duke of Gaogui Township?"
translations.idiomatic: Chun shot back: "Where is the Duke of Gaogui Township?"

sentences.zh: 充慚怒，上表解職；

translations.literal: Chong, ashamed and angry, memorialized to resign office;
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Chong memorialized to resign;

sentences.zh: 純亦上表自劾。

translations.literal: Chun also memorialized to impeach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chun impeached himself as well.

sentences.zh: 詔免純官，仍下五府正其臧否。

translations.literal: An edict removed Chun from office and still sent the matter to the Five Offices to judge his merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: The court dismissed Chun and referred both men to the Five Offices for judgment.

sentences.zh: 石苞以爲純榮官忘親，當除名，齊王攸等以爲純於禮律未有違。

translations.literal: Shi Bao thought Chun had honored office and forgotten kin and ought to be struck from the rolls; Prince You of Qi and others thought Chun had not violated ritual law.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao argued Chun had abandoned his parents for office and should be struck from the rolls; Prince Qi Sima You held he had broken no law.

sentences.zh: 詔從攸議，復以純爲國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The edict followed You's opinion and again made Chun Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Sima You and restored Chun as director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 呉主之遊華里也，右丞相萬彧與右大司馬丁奉、左將軍留平密謀曰：「若至華里不歸，社稷事重，不得不自還。」

translations.literal: When the Lord of Wu toured Huali, Right Chancellor Wan Yu with Right Grand Marshal Ding Feng and Left General Liu Ping secretly plotted, saying, "If we reach Huali and do not return, the altars' affairs are weighty—we must return ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: During Sun Hao's tour of Huali, right chancellor Wan Yu, right grand marshal Ding Feng, and left general Liu Ping plotted: "If he reaches Huali and does not return, we must bring the court home ourselves."

sentences.zh: 呉主頗聞之，以彧等舊臣，隱忍不發。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu somewhat heard of it; because Yu and the others were old ministers, he restrained himself and did not expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao heard rumors but, treating them as veteran ministers, held his anger in check.

sentences.zh: 是歳，呉主因會，以毒酒飲彧，傳酒人私減之。

translations.literal: That year, at a gathering the Lord of Wu made Yu drink poisoned wine; the wine-server privately reduced it.
translations.idiomatic: That year at a banquet Sun Hao gave Yu poisoned wine; the server secretly diluted it.

sentences.zh: 又飲留平，平覺之，服他藥以解，得不死。

translations.literal: He also made Liu Ping drink; Ping perceived it and took other medicine to counteract it and was not killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then tried Liu Ping, who sensed the poison, took an antidote, and survived.

sentences.zh: 彧自殺；

translations.literal: Yu killed himself;
translations.idiomatic: Yu killed himself;

sentences.zh: 平憂懣，月餘亦死。

translations.literal: Ping, worried and distressed, also died after more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, crushed by grief, died within a month.

sentences.zh: 徙彧子弟於廬陵。

translations.literal: Yu's sons and younger brothers were moved to Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's family was exiled to Luling.

sentences.zh: 初，彧請選忠淸之士以補近職，呉主以大司農樓玄爲宮下鎭，主殿中事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu had requested selecting loyal and pure gentlemen to fill close offices; the Lord of Wu made Grand Minister of Agriculture Lou Xuan palace commander below, in charge of palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu had urged appointing upright men to court posts; Sun Hao made grand minister Lou Xuan palace commander overseeing the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 玄正身帥衆，奉法而行，應對切直，呉主浸不悅。

translations.literal: Xuan corrected his person and led the masses, followed the law in action, and answered directly and bluntly; the Lord of Wu gradually disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan led by example and spoke plainly; Sun Hao grew to dislike him.

sentences.zh: 中書令領太子太傅賀邵上疎諫曰：「自頃年以來，朝列紛錯，眞偽相貿，忠良排墜，信臣被害。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary and Crown Prince Grand Tutor He Shao submitted a remonstrance, saying, "In recent years the court ranks have been confused, true and false traded places, the loyal and good pushed down, and trusted ministers harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace secretary and crown prince tutor He Shao memorialized: "In recent years court ranks have tangled, the loyal have been cast down, and trusted ministers destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是以正士摧方而庸臣苟媚，先意承指，各希時趣。

translations.literal: Therefore upright gentlemen have their squareness broken while mediocre ministers fawn, anticipating intent and following fingers, each hoping for the fashion of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men are broken while flatterers anticipate your every whim.

sentences.zh: 人執反理之評，士吐詭道之論，遂使淸流變濁，忠臣結舌。

translations.literal: People hold judgments against reason; gentlemen utter crooked discourse—thus the clear stream turns turbid and loyal ministers bite their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Reason is reversed and loyal tongues are silenced—the clear stream has turned foul.

sentences.zh: 陛下處九天之上，隱百里之室，言出風靡，令行景從。

translations.literal: Your Majesty stands above the nine heavens and is hidden in a chamber a hundred li away; words go forth like wind, orders move like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sits above the nine heavens, hidden a hundred li deep; your word is wind, your command shadow.

sentences.zh: 親洽寵媚之臣，日聞順意之辭，將謂此輩實賢而天下已平也。

translations.literal: Daily you hear the words of fawning favorites and will think these men truly worthy and All Under Heaven already at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Daily you hear sycophants and will think the realm already at peace.

sentences.zh: 臣聞興國之君樂聞其過，荒亂之主樂聞其譽；

translations.literal: I have heard that lords who raise states delight to hear their faults, while lords of waste and disorder delight to hear their praise;
translations.idiomatic: Sagely rulers love to hear their faults; ruined rulers love praise alone.

sentences.zh: 聞其過者過日消而福臻，聞其譽者譽日損而禍至。

translations.literal: those who hear faults see faults daily diminish and blessing arrive; those who hear praise see praise daily diminish and calamity come.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing faults diminishes faults and brings blessing; hearing praise diminishes virtue and brings calamity.

sentences.zh: 陛下嚴刑法以禁直辭，黜善士以逆諫口，杯酒造次，死生不保，仕者以退爲幸，居者以出爲福，誠非所以保光洪緒，熙隆道化也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty uses severe punishments to forbid straight words, dismisses good gentlemen to block remonstrance, and with a cup of wine in passing, life and death are not secure—those in office take retirement as fortune and those at home take departure as blessing. This is truly not the means to preserve the great succession and brighten and uplift the Way's transformation.
translations.idiomatic: You forbid honest speech with harsh law, drive away good men, and with a cup of wine decide life or death—officials pray to retire, commoners pray to flee. This cannot preserve the dynasty or uplift the realm.

sentences.zh: 何定本僕隸小人，身無行能，而陛下愛其佞媚，假以威福。

translations.literal: He Ding was originally a menial slave, himself without conduct or ability, yet Your Majesty loves his fawning and flatters and lends him prestige and favor.
translations.idiomatic: He Ding was a menial slave without ability, yet Your Majesty favors his flattery and grants him power.

sentences.zh: 夫小人求入，必進奸利。

translations.literal: When petty men seek entry, they are certain to advance treacherous profit.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men who seek favor always bring treachery in their train.

sentences.zh: 定間者忘興事役，發江邊戍兵以驅麋鹿，老弱饑凍，大小怨歎。

translations.literal: Ding of late forgot to raise public works, sent river-border garrison troops to drive elk and deer—the old and weak starved and froze, great and small groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Ding lately diverted border garrisons to hunt elk—the aged froze and starved, and the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『國之興也，視民如赤子；

translations.literal: The Documents say, 'When a state rises, it regards the people as infants;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'When a state rises, it treats the people as infants;

sentences.zh: 其亡也，以民爲草芥。』

translations.literal: when it perishes, it treats the people as grass and stalks.'
translations.idiomatic: when it falls, it treats them as weeds.'

sentences.zh: 今法禁轉苛，賦調益繁，中官、近臣所在興事，而長吏畏罪，苦民求辦。

translations.literal: Now prohibitions grow harsher and levies more numerous; inner attendants and close ministers raise projects everywhere, while chief officials, fearing guilt, torment the people to fulfill tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Laws grow crueler and taxes heavier; palace agents launch projects everywhere while terrified magistrates squeeze the people to deliver.

sentences.zh: 是以人力不堪，家戸離散，呼嗟之聲，感傷和氣。

translations.literal: Therefore human strength cannot bear it, households scatter in separation, and the sound of sighing wounds harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Strength fails, families scatter, and the people's sighs poison the realm's harmony.

sentences.zh: 今國無一年之儲，家無經月之蓄，而後宮之中坐食者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Now the state has not a year's store, families not a month's reserve, yet within the rear palace more than ten thousand sit idle at their meals.
translations.idiomatic: The state lacks a year's stores, families a month's grain, yet more than ten thousand palace women eat without labor.

sentences.zh: 又，北敵注目，伺國盛衰，長江之限，不可久恃，苟我不能守，一葦可杭也。

translations.literal: Moreover the northern enemy fixes his gaze, watching whether the state waxes or wanes; the Yangzi's barrier cannot long be relied on—if we cannot defend it, a single reed can cross it.
translations.idiomatic: The northern foe watches our strength; the Yangtze barrier will not hold forever—if we fail to defend it, a reed raft will carry the enemy across.

sentences.zh: 願陛下豐基強本，割情從道，則成、康之治興，聖祖之祚隆矣！」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will enrich the foundation and strengthen the root, cut off private feeling and follow the Way—then the governance of Cheng and Kang will rise and the blessed seat of the holy ancestor will be exalted!"
translations.idiomatic: Enrich the foundation, follow the Way, and the age of Cheng and Kang may return—the holy ancestor's throne will endure!"

sentences.zh: 呉主深恨之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 於是左右共誣樓玄、賀邵相逢，駐共耳語大笑，謗訕政事，倶被詰責。

translations.literal: Thereupon the attendants together slandered Lou Xuan and He Shao, saying that when they met they stopped and whispered ear to ear and laughed loudly, maligning government affairs, and both were interrogated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Court flatterers claimed Lou Xuan and He Shao had met, whispered, and mocked policy; both were interrogated.

sentences.zh: 送玄付廣州，邵原復職。

translations.literal: Xuan was sent to Guangzhou; Shao was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was sent to Guangzhou; Shao briefly kept his post.

sentences.zh: 旣而復徙玄於交趾，竟殺之。

translations.literal: Soon Xuan was again moved to Jiaozhi and in the end was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xuan was moved to Jiaozhi and killed.

sentences.zh: 久之，何定奸穢發聞，亦伏誅。

translations.literal: After a long while, He Ding's treacherous filth was exposed and heard, and he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In time He Ding's crimes surfaced and he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 羊祜歸自江陵，務修德信以懷呉人。

translations.literal: Yang Hu returned from Jiangling and devoted himself to cultivating virtue and trust to win over the people of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Jiangling, Yang Hu cultivated virtue and trust to win Wu hearts.

sentences.zh: 毎交兵，刻日方戰，不爲掩襲之計。

translations.literal: Whenever they crossed arms in battle, they fixed a day to fight and made no plans for surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever armies met, he fixed a day for battle and forbade surprise attacks.

sentences.zh: 將帥有欲進譎計者，輒飲以醇酒，使不得言。

translations.literal: When generals wished to advance deceitful plans, he would give them strong wine to drink so they could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who proposed stratagems he plied with wine until they fell silent.

sentences.zh: 祜出軍行呉境，刈穀爲糧，皆計所侵，送絹償之。

translations.literal: When Hu led troops through Wu territory and reaped grain for provisions, he calculated what was taken and sent silk to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: Marching through Wu he requisitioned grain but paid for every measure in silk.

sentences.zh: 毎會衆江、沔遊獵，常止晉地，若禽獸先爲呉人所傷而爲晉兵所得者，皆送還之。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered the masses to hunt on the Jiang and Han, he always stopped on Jin territory; if game had first been wounded by Wu men but taken by Jin troops, all were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting on the Jiang and Han he kept to Jin ground and returned game first wounded by Wu.

sentences.zh: 於是呉邊人皆悅服。

translations.literal: Thereupon the border people of Wu all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu border folk submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 祜與陸抗對境，使命常通。

translations.literal: Hu and Lu Kang faced one another across the border; envoys constantly passed.
translations.idiomatic: Facing Lu Kang across the border, Yang Hu exchanged envoys freely.

sentences.zh: 抗遺祜酒，祜飲之不疑；

translations.literal: Kang sent Hu wine; Hu drank it without doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Kang sent wine; Hu drank without suspicion;

sentences.zh: 抗疾，求藥於祜，祜以成藥與之，抗卽服之。

translations.literal: when Kang fell ill he sought medicine from Hu, and Hu gave him prepared medicine; Kang at once took it.
translations.idiomatic: when Kang fell ill he asked Yang Hu for medicine and took the dose Hu sent at once.

sentences.zh: 人多諫抗，抗曰：「豈有鴆人羊叔子哉！」

translations.literal: Many remonstrated with Kang; Kang said, "Could there be a poisoner in Uncle Yang!"
translations.idiomatic: Advisers protested; Kang said: "Would Uncle Yang poison me?"

sentences.zh: 抗告其邊戍曰：「彼專爲德，我專爲暴，是不戰而自服也。

translations.literal: Kang told his border garrisons, "They specialize in virtue, we specialize in violence—this is not fighting but making them submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He told his border troops: "They practice virtue, we practice violence—we defeat ourselves without fighting.

sentences.zh: 各保分界而已，無求細利。」

translations.literal: Each keep to the boundary—that is all; do not seek petty profit."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the line and seek no petty gain."

sentences.zh: 呉主聞二境交和，以詰抗，抗曰：「一邑一鄕不可以無信義，況大國乎！

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu heard the two borders were at harmony and questioned Kang; Kang said, "One town or one village cannot be without trust and righteousness—how much less a great state!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao questioned the truce; Kang answered: "Even a village needs trust—how much more a great state!

sentences.zh: 臣不如此，正是彰其德，於祜無傷也。」

translations.literal: If I did not act thus, I would only display their virtue, and Hu would suffer no harm."
translations.idiomatic: By matching his courtesy I only display his virtue—it harms Yang Hu not at all."

sentences.zh: 呉主用諸將之謀，數侵盜晉邊。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu followed the generals' plans and repeatedly raided and stole on the Jin border.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao followed his generals and raided the Jin frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 陸抗上疎曰：「昔有夏多罪而殷湯用師，紂作淫虐而周武授鉞。

translations.literal: Lu Kang submitted a memorial, saying, "Formerly Xia had many crimes and Tang of Yin used troops; Zhou made licentious cruelty and Wu of Zhou received the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang memorialized: "When Xia sinned, Tang of Yin marched; when Zhou tyrannized, King Wu of Zhou struck.

sentences.zh: 苟無其時，雖復大聖，亦宜養威自保，不可輕動也。

translations.literal: If there is not the time for it, even if one restores a great sage, he ought to nurture prestige and protect himself and cannot lightly move.
translations.idiomatic: Without the proper moment, even a sage must husband strength and hold still.

sentences.zh: 今不務力農富國，審官任能，明黜陟，愼刑賞，訓諸司以德，撫百姓以仁，而聽諸將徇名，窮兵黷武，動費萬計，士卒調瘁，寇不爲衰而我已大病矣。

translations.literal: Now you do not exert effort to enrich the state through agriculture, examine offices and employ the able, clarify demotion and promotion, be cautious in punishments and rewards, instruct the various offices with virtue, and soothe the hundred surnames with benevolence, but listen to generals who pursue fame, exhaust the army in repeated campaigns, move and spend by the ten thousands, soldiers are worn and distressed, the bandits are not weakened while we already have grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you neglect farming, appointments, rewards, and kindness to the people, and heed generals who crave glory—campaigns drain the treasury, troops are exhausted, the enemy is unbroken, and we are already gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 今爭帝王之資而昧十百之利，此人臣之奸便，非國家之良策也！

translations.literal: Now to contend for the capital of emperor and king while obscuring profit of ten or a hundred—this is the treacherous convenience of ministers, not the good strategy of the state!
translations.idiomatic: To fight for imperial dominion while chasing petty gains is ministers' treachery, not statecraft!

sentences.zh: 昔齊、魯三戰，魯人再克，而亡不旋踵。

translations.literal: Formerly Qi and Lu fought three battles; the men of Lu twice prevailed, yet perished without turning heel.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Lu fought three times; Lu won twice yet perished swiftly.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 大小之勢異也。

translations.literal: The disparity of great and small was different.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small were not equal.

sentences.zh: 況今師所克獲，不補所喪哉？」

translations.literal: How much less when what our army captures today does not make up for what we lose!"
translations.idiomatic: How much less when today's gains cannot repay today's losses!"

sentences.zh: 呉主不從。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 羊祜不附結中朝權貴，荀勗、馮紞之徒皆惡之。

translations.literal: Yang Hu did not attach himself to the powerful at court; Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and their sort all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu shunned court factions; Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and their clique hated him.

sentences.zh: 從甥王衍嘗詣祜陳事，辭甚淸辯；

translations.literal: His sister's son Wang Yan once came to Hu to state affairs; his words were very clear and eloquent;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wang Yan once presented a case with fluent eloquence;

sentences.zh: 祜不然之，衍拂衣去。

translations.literal: Hu did not approve; Yan brushed his robe and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hu disapproved; Yan stormed out.

sentences.zh: 祜顧謂賓客曰：「王夷甫方當以盛名處大位，然敗俗傷化，必此人也。」

translations.literal: Hu turned to his guests and said, "Wang Yifu will certainly occupy a great post with a famous reputation, yet he will ruin custom and harm transformation—it will surely be this man."
translations.idiomatic: Hu told his guests: "Wang Yifu will win fame and high office—and ruin the age."

sentences.zh: 及攻江陵，祜以軍法將斬王戎。

translations.literal: When attacking Jiangling, Hu was about to execute Wang Rong by military law.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiangling campaign Hu nearly executed Wang Rong by martial law.

sentences.zh: 衍，戎之從弟也，故二人皆憾之，言論多毀祜，時人爲之語曰：「二王當國，羊公無德。」」

translations.literal: Yan was Rong's younger cousin by the father's line, and therefore the two men both resented him; their talk often slandered Hu, and men of the time made a saying of it: "When the two Wangs hold the state, Duke Yang has no virtue."”
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Rong's cousin; both resented Hu and slandered him until people said: "When the two Wangs rule, Duke Yang has no virtue."”
